Sir,

The following noteworthy events have occurred on and
since the morning of June 5:-

EXTENSION OF THE STRIKE.

Further large numbers of Chinese employees of foreign
concerns joined in the general strike on June 5, whilst an
increasing number of workers in Chinese employ have also gone
on strike. In several plants, fairly large numbers of strikers
have, however, resumed work and it is obvious that many others
would do likewise were it not for the effect of intimidation.

1480 employees, mostly women, of the Wei Tung Cotton Mill
(Chinese) 12, Lay Road, struck work on June 5 and 300 women
walked out of the Sung Sing Cotton Mill (Chinese) 78 Ward Road.

150 men employed at the Presbyterian Mission Press, 155
North Szechuen Road Extension (Outside Limits) failed to
appear for work at 7 a.m. June 5.

By 2 p.m. June 5 practically all employees of the British
Cigarette Co.'s factory at 56 Dixwell Road had struck work
increasing the total number of strikers from this plant to 350.

All employees of the Ching Yuin Silk Weaving Co.'s
factory (Chinese) 400 Chaoufeong Road, struck work on the
morning of June 5. They consist of 120 men and about 80
women. 36 workers from the same company's godown at 586
Yochow Road also went on strike.

先生，

自6月5日上午以来，发生了以下值得注意的事件：

罢工的蔓延。

6月5日，更多外商企业的中国雇员加入了总罢工，同时受雇于华商企业的工人中也有越来越多的人参加罢工。然而，在几家工厂中，相当数量的罢工者已经复工，显然如果不是因为受到恐吓的影响，许多其他人也会这样做。

位于雷路（Lay Road）12号的纬通纱厂（华资）的1480名雇员（大多为女性）于6月5日罢工，300名女工离开了位于华德路（Ward Road）78号的宋兴纱厂（华资）。

截至6月5日下午2时，位于狄思威路（Dixwell Road）56号的英商烟草公司工厂的几乎所有雇员都已罢工，使该厂的罢工总人数达到350人。

位于兆丰路（Chaoufeong Road）400号的清源丝织厂（华资）的所有雇员于6月5日上午罢工。其中包括120名男工和约80名女工。该公司位于姚家渡路（Yochow Road）586号栈房的36名工人也参加了罢工。

Nearly all the Chinese servants at the Burlington Hotel to the number of about 70, walked out at 2 p.m. June 5.

Some of the striking office employees of the P. and O.
Bank, the American-Oriental Bank and the Banque Sino-Belge
are expected to return to work on the morning of June 6. A
piece of lead was thrown through a window of the Compradore
Office of the Chartered Bank at 2.45 p.m. June 5 and the
Compradore has received a letter by mail threatening that he
will be shot if his staff continues to work.

53 Chinese banks and exchange shops in Central District
remain closed but carry on business through back doors, side
doors or grille windows.

Compradores of nearly all large foreign firms in Central
District have received threatening letters urging them and their
staffs to discontinue working for foreigners. In many cases
the postage on these missives has to be paid by the addressees.

25 fitters and coolies of the China General Omnibus Co.
Connaught Road, walked out at 11 a.m. June 5. All conductors
reported for duty on June 5. Only No. 9 Route is being served
(Avenue Road, Avenue Edward VII. and Avenue Foch between 12
noon and 2 p.m. and 4 p.m. to 6 p.m.) each bus being guarded
by a member of the Shot Gun Corps.

All students of the Southern University, 44 Markham Road,
and of the Great China University, 201 Ferry Road, have vacated
the premises of the institutions.

60 men from the Asiatic Engineering Works (U.S.) 130 East
Yuhang Road and about 400 from the P.W.D. workshops in Wayside
are now on strike.

位于余杭路（East Yuhang Road）130号的亚细亚工程公司（Asiatic Engineering Works，美资）的60名工人和位于韦尔斯利路（Wayside）工务局车间的约400名工人目前正在罢工。

Market conditions in Wayside have improved.
Determined attempts were made on the morning of June 5
to intimidate the few remaining stall holders in the Wuchow

Markets in general are carrying on about half normal
pressure.
All Chinese shops throughout the Settlement remain

ASSAULTS ON JAPANESE AND OTHER FOREIGNERS.
Throughout the day, June 5, these were practically
negligible in the Settlement.
About 8.15 p.m. June 5 a stone was thrown at a foreigner

standing on Jukong Road on both sides of the North Szechuen Road
Extension. They hastily loaded their rifles and in the
excitement one of them fired a shot into the air which so
alarmed his comrades that they scampered off in all directions
into Chapel.

Shanghai, June 6, 1925.
Bulletin of Incidents connected with the General Strike.

A Chinese Police Constable wearing a long gown
over his uniform was seen removing Municipal proclamations
on Nanking Road at 2 p.m. June 5 by a member of the
Police Special Reserve (J. J. Keegan). The latter seems
to have been at a loss as to how he should act and
allowed the culprit to escape. Report by C.D.I. Reeves.

The foreign accountant of the Shanghai Mutual
Telephone Co., Mr. E. R. Palmer, has stated that several
Chinese telephone operators have expressed their
willingness to resume work, but the management declines
to allow them to go back. Report received by C.D.I. Reeves.

~~Dr. Max Kindler,~~ an ex-Austrian of very unsavoury
reputation, who is now serving in the Police Special Reserve
reports that he has seen letters showing that Messrs. Musso
and Fischer have done some service for the Soviet which
has won them the approbation of Karachan, the Soviet
Minister. Kindler is of the opinion that Messrs. Musso
and Fischer are now working on behalf of the Soviet to
further the present anti-foreign movement. C. D. I. Reeves report

Detectives inquiries indicate that the report in
the Russian Press to the effect that an assault had been
perpetrated by a crowd of Chinese upon Russians in Chapei
is entirely without foundation. The allegation that a
Chinese was killed in the alleged affray is equally untrue.
Billets have been found in the Astor House for the Russians
alleged to have been concerned in the supposed incident.
No corroboration can be found of the suggestion that
Dolgorakoff, the benefactor of these Russians, has sympathy
with the parties concerned in the present anti-foreign
movement. C. D. I. Reeves report

上海，1925年6月6日。
与总罢工有关的事件简报。

6月5日下午2时，一名身穿长袍罩在制服外的华籍巡捕在南京路撕除工部局告示，被警务处特别后备队队员（J. J. Keegan）目睹。后者似乎不知该如何行动，让肇事者逃脱。由刑事调查主任里夫斯（C.D.I. Reeves）报告。

上海电话互助公司（Shanghai Mutual Telephone Co.）的外籍会计师 E. R. Palmer 先生表示，几名中国电话接线员已表示愿意复工，但管理层拒绝让他们回去。由刑事调查主任里夫斯收到的报告。

~~马克斯·金德勒博士（Dr. Max Kindler）~~，一名声誉极差的奥地利前公民，目前在警务处特别后备队服役，他报告称看到信件显示穆索（Musso）和费舍尔（Fischer）两位先生曾为苏维埃提供过一些服务，从而赢得了苏维埃部长卡拉汉（Karachan）的赞许。金德勒认为，穆索和费舍尔两位先生现在正代表苏维埃行事，以推动当前的反外运动。刑事调查主任里夫斯报告

侦探调查显示，俄文报刊中关于一群中国人在闸北袭击俄罗斯人的报道完全毫无根据。所谓在 alleged 斗殴中有一名中国人被杀的指控同样不实。据称卷入这一假设事件的俄罗斯人已在礼查饭店（Astor House）找到了住处。没有任何证据可以证实以下说法：这些俄罗斯人的资助人多尔戈拉科夫（Dolgorakoff）同情当前反外运动的相关各方。刑事调查主任里夫斯报告

A student of Nanyang University, a Government school
at No. 863 Avenue Haig, was caught by Police on Great
Western Road at 3 p.m. June 5 whilst endeavouring to
persuade P.W.D. coolies to strike.

It is rumoured that three officers of the Bolshevik
Red Army will arrive shortly in Shanghai to assist in a
campaign being organized by the Soviet with a view to
aggravating the anti-foreign feelings of the students and
agitators.

Col. Chang Ts Ying, Chief of the Shanghai and Woosung
Constabulary, on the afternoon of June 5 detailed thirty
armed gendarmes to Pootung to protect foreign firms there.

A general strike has been declared by the workers of
the Sung Sing (宋兴) Cotton Mill, (Chinese), No. 2
Iohang Road. Some 2,290 workers are involved. Most of
these reside in Chapei, where intimidation is rife.

A Chinese named Loh Zien Foh (陸錢福), No. 303
Wuchow Road, was at 9 p.m. June 5 assaulted on that
thoroughfare by a crowd of one hundred and fifty loafers
who accused him of wearing a hat made in Japan.

Students to the number of 1,500 who were holding a
demonstration on a piece of vacant ground near the junction
of Dixwell and Urga Roads in June 5 were dispersed by an armoured car,
whose crew thought the place where the demonstration was
being held was within the Settlement.

Two coolies who live at 155 Ningpo Road and a shop
assistant who lives at 196 Ningpo Road were arrested and
charged at 9 p.m. 5/6/25 for posting pamphlets.

有谣言称，三名布尔什维克红军军官即将抵达上海，协助苏维埃组织的一场旨在加剧学生和煽动者反外情绪的运动。

6月5日下午，上海与吴淞警察局局长张子英（Chang Ts Ying，音译）上校派遣三十名武装宪兵前往浦东，保护那里的外商企业。

位于耀华路（Iohang Road）2号的宋兴纱厂（华资）工人宣布举行总罢工。涉及工人约2,290人。这些人大多居住在闸北，那里恐吓行为盛行。

REPORT ON_______________________________________________________________________________________

        Between 2 p.m. and 4 p.m. February 24th, 1925 a meeting of
between 20 and 30 representatives of the strikers was held at the
Labour Union Headquarters, Chapel, behind closed doors. It was
passed that the 20 cents per day which had been promised to the
strikers would be paid to the officials and representatives only.
        About 5 p.m. February 22nd, 1925 a Chinese female named
Wong Siau Mei (王 小 妹) alias Wong An Ching (王 阿 金) age 21
years, Cantonese, and a Chinese male giving the name of Koo Ling
Tsang (顧 順 章) native of Woosung employed with the B.A.T. Poo-
tung came to this Station with some food to give to Sung Liang Wei
(in custody at the Ching Tsa Ting), they understanding that he was
locked up at this Station. They were subjected to lengthy ques-
tioning as to their connection with Sung Liang Wei but were very
reluctant to answer, the man stated he did not know him and had
only accompanied his friend to this Station, the woman stated she
only knew Sung through working with his wife in a stocking factory.
        They made several contradictory statements as to their
business, addresses etc. but as they were not recognised by any of
our informers as having been seen during the strike were allowed
to go. On leaving the Station they were followed and eventually
went into the Nyi Ping Lee (義 品 里), Jukong Road, O. O. L. on the
West Side of North Szechuen Road. The woman went into a small school
No. 468 Nyi Ping Lee, known as the Zang Tsu School (尚 志 學 堂), the
man went into another school at No. 465 Nyi Ping Lee, known as the
Chau Yang School (教 養 學 堂).
        Enquiries proceeding.

        1925年2月24日下午2时至4时之间，20至30名罢工代表在位于小教堂（Chapel）后面的工会总部举行了一次闭门会议。会议决定，此前承诺给罢工者的每天20美分津贴，仅支付给官员和代表。
        1925年2月22日下午5时许，一名名叫王小妹（Wong Siau Mei），又名王阿金（Wong An Ching）的21岁广东籍中国女子，以及一名自称顾顺章（Koo Ling Tsang）、吴淞人、受雇于英美烟草公司浦东分公司的中国男子，带着食物来到本分局，欲送给孙良卫（Sung Liang Wei）（当时被拘押在警察厅），他们误以为孙被关押在本分局。他们就其与孙良卫的关系接受了长时间讯问，但非常不愿回答；该男子称他不认识孙，只是陪朋友来分局；该女子称她只因与孙的妻子在一家袜厂共事而认识孙。
        他们就其职业、住址等事宜作了多处自相矛盾的陈述，但由于我们的线人并未认出他们在罢工期间出现过，故准许其离开。离开分局后，他们受到跟踪，最终进入北四川路西侧的义品里（Nyi Ping Lee）。该女子进入了义品里468号的一所名为尚志学堂（Zang Tsu School）的小学校，该男子则进入了义品里465号的另一所名为教养学堂（Chau Yang School）的学校。

（批：Holed & recommended this memo be filed 1/8）

FROM THE POLICE FORCE,
MUNICIPAL COUNCIL.
POOTOO ROAD STATION.
Shanghai, 15th Oct., 193... To The Director of Criminal
Investigation.

Sir,

I respectfully beg to recommend U.P.C. No. ... for conspicuous bravery on the morning of February 10th, 1930.
This man, one Sikh and one Chinese Constables was with me on the above date when about 400 rioters attacked No. 10 & 14 Mills, beat up the Japanese employees and were wrecking the mills when we came on the scene. We were obliged to use force, with the result that ... rioters, in a few minutes, something eight or ten being arrested. ... 10 others were convicted on the 14-7-30, being sentenced to 60 days imprisonment or a fine of $50.00. I am quite satisfied that their early arrival on the scene and subsequent action saved a dangerous situation.

W
H.

Yours sincerely,
J. Foley.
Inspector I.C.

上海，193...年10月15日。致刑事侦缉处处长。

先生，

我谨建议授予警员编号 ... 以表彰其在1930年2月10日上午的英勇表现。
当日，该名锡克族警员和一名华捕与我在一起，当时约400名暴徒袭击了10号和14号工厂，殴打日本雇员并破坏工厂设施，当我们赶到现场时。我们被迫使用武力，结果在几分钟内逮捕了约八至十名暴徒。... 另外10人于1930年7月14日被定罪，判处60天监禁或罚款50.00美元。我完全确信，他们的及时到达和随后的行动挽救了危险局势。

W
H.

此致，
J. Foley.
刑事侦缉督察。

March 21st 1925.
REPORT ON Release of Sung Liang Wei (孫良衛) by the Ching Tsa
Ting (警察廳) Authorities.
Made by D. S. Toshio. Forwarded by J. Eoly Insp.
Sir:-
I beg to report that at 11 a.m. March 17th 1925, an applica-
tion was made to the Ching Tsa Ting (警察廳) Authorities for the
extradition of one Sung Liang Wei (孫良衛), a leading agitator in
the recent cotton mills strike, who was arrested in Chapel on Febru-
ary 19th 1925 at the instance of this Station, on a charge of inti-
midation. Previous applications had been made without success.
Armed with the necessary extradition papers, we were again informed
that no decision had yet been arrived at in connection with the case.
At 10-30 a.m. March 20th 1925 a further application for
Sung Liang Wei's extradition was made when we were informed that he
had been released on March 16th 1925 by order of the Chief of Police,
at the request of representatives of the Chinese General Chamber of
Commerce and the Japanese Mill owners, so that when we were told on
March 17th that no decision had been arrived at, the man had already
been released. At 5-30 p.m. March 20th 1925, Zee Ko Seng (徐可陞),
General Secretary of the Chinese General Chamber of Commerce, in an
interview at his office, informed us that he had been in charge of
negotiations, on behalf of the Chamber of Commerce, in connection
with the recent labour trouble, that his last visit to the Ching Tsa
Ting was on March 16th 1925, & that he was unaware that Sung Liang
Wei had been released until he was informed by Chief Detective
Inspector Givens over the telephone on the morning of March 20th
1925. He further stated that the Chamber of Commerce did not go
security, and are in no way responsible for the man.
Mr. Okada of the Nagaai Wata Kaisha Company was unaware that
Sung Liang Wei had been released, and he does not know of any request

由 D. S. Toshio 撰写。由 J. Eoly 督察转呈。
先生：
谨此报告，1925年3月17日上午11时，向警察厅当局申请引渡孙良卫（孫良衛），他是近期棉纺厂罢工的主要煽动者，曾于1925年2月19日应本分局要求在小教堂（Chapel）以恐吓罪被捕。此前曾多次申请未果。当我们持必要的引渡文件再次前往时，又被告知该案尚未作出决定。
1925年3月20日上午10时30分，再次申请引渡孙良卫时，我们获悉他已根据警察总监的命令，应中国总商会代表和日本厂主的要求，于1925年3月16日获释。因此，当我们在3月17日被告知尚未作出决定时，此人实际上已被释放。1925年3月20日下午5时30分，中国总商会秘书长徐可陞（Zee Ko Seng）在其办公室接受面谈时告知我们，他代表商会负责处理近期的劳资纠纷谈判，他最后一次访问警察厅是在1925年3月16日，直到1925年3月20日上午接到刑事侦缉高级督察吉文斯（Givens）的电话通知，他才得知孙良卫已被释放。他还表示，商会并未提供担保，对此人不承担任何责任。
内外棉株式会社的冈田先生（Mr. Okada）不知道孙良卫已被释放，也不知道有任何请求

Apart from the student Tsang Yung, a student at the Dah Hwa

further application for him was made on March 12th 1925 but without
success.
The Ching Tsa Ting Authorities stating that they have not
decided what action they will take in the matter.
A further report will be forwarded in this connection.

I am, Sir,

REPORT ON Stoppage of work at the Naigai Wata Kaisha No. 5 Mill.

Made by D. S. Forkin. Forwarded by J. Foley Insp.

Sir:-

I beg to report that at 7.50 a.m. March 3rd, 1925 a telephone message was received from Mr. Motoki of the Naigai Wata Kaisha Company reporting that the employees of their No. 5 Mill, West Soochow Road were damaging the machinery. All available men under Inspector Foley immediately proceeded there and found that all the sixty frames in the Ring Spinning Department had been dislocated and all work in that department stopped, the floor was littered with bobbins, cotton, broken electric bulbs, lamp shades, glass from the roof and a broken clock. From enquiries made it was ascertained that 103 males, mostly boys between 14 and 17 years of age and 54 females started work in this department at 6 a.m. March 3rd. All went well until about 7.40 a.m. when one of the forewomen had occasion to speak to one of the boys owing to him getting behind in his work in not having empty bobbins in readiness to replace the full ones. This boy became abusive to the forewoman and told her that other mills employed boys specially for that work, also that the Naigai Wata Kaisha Company had not paid any gratuity to the hands on resuming work after the strike as other firms had done. The boy, joined by six or seven other male workers went to the Chinese foreman to report the incident, but the foreman who was a substitute did not give them any satisfaction and told them to wait until the regular foreman returned to work. These workers becoming angered by the attitude of the foreman collected almost all the other male workers together and commenced to smash up the machinery etc., the damage being estimated by the management at $1,242.42 to machinery and $117.05 to electric fittings, windows etc. In view of all the

Sir:-

Further, I beg to forward a report on the following points in connection with the labour unrest in the Pootoo Road district during the month of February 1925:-

1. The Western District Working Men's Day & Night School, Nos. 781, 791, & 793 Penang Road, three Chinese Houses which were once the Headquarters of the Naigai Wata Kaisha Labourers Union. Two of the houses were broken through to make a school room, the other one was used as a recreation room. The pupils attending the school paid ten cents per month, and workers using the recreation room paid the same amount. The students of the Shanghai University and the Southern University are said to have been teachers (without salary) at the school and no doubt preached their communist ideas.

About a week before the strike the Headquarters were removed from Penang Road to San Tun Lee (三德里), Chapel, in rear of the Dai Tong Cotton Mill which is the Labour Union present headquarters. Two friends of Sung Liang Wei (宋良威), a leading agitator, were seen to enter two Chinese schools on Dukong Road, Chapel, one a female went into the Zang Tsau School (尚志學堂), situated at No. 446 Ayl Ping Lee (義品里), the other a male, went into the Chen Yung School (教養學堂) No. 440 Ayl Ping Lee.

1. 西区工人日夜学校，位于槟榔路781、791及793号，这三栋中式房屋曾是内外棉株式会社工人工会的总部。其中两栋房屋被打通作为教室，另一栋用作娱乐室。就读该校的学生每月缴纳一角钱，使用娱乐室的工人也缴纳相同金额。据称，上海大学和南方大学的学生曾在该校担任教师（无薪），无疑宣扬了他们的共产主义思想。

罢工前约一周，总部从槟榔路迁至三德里（San Tun Lee），位于大通纱厂后面的教堂，此处现为工会总部。有人看到主要煽动者宋良威（Sung Liang Wei）的两名朋友进入杜孔路（Dukong Road）教堂的两所中文学校，其中一名女性进入了位于义品里（Ayl Ping Lee）446号的尚志学堂（Zang Tsau School），另一名男性进入了位于义品里440号的教养学堂（Chen Yung School）。

2. 1925年2月2日，40名男性雇员因不服从命令而被解雇，随后6名工人因恐吓罪被捕并被判处监禁3周。

一名在租界骚乱期间被捕的学生属于罗宾森路（Robinson Road）的大夏大学，但针对他的证据相当薄弱，且该大学与此次劳工纠纷无任何其他关联。

of attacking the Japanese owned mills, again the early arrival of
all available men under Inspector Foley and reinforcements from the

to state that we struck work several days ago and we have received no

and who are willing to be the foreigners' dogs.

                                    You do not stand on principal

REPORT ON Strike Situation.

Made by D. S. FORBES.          Forwarded by J. G. L. Snape.

Sir:-
    In connection with the labour unrest in the Pootoo area
district, I beg to report that the Nippon Yarn Weaving Company opened
their mills to the workers at 6 a.m. February 28th 1925, after an
agreement had been signed between representatives of the employers
and the operatives at the Chinese General Chamber of Commerce about
7 p.m. on February 27th 1925. The usual police precautions were
taken for the protection of the workers and no signs of complaints
were received at this Section. The district can be regarded as
quiet.
    About 60% of the company's day employees turned up at the
mills but owing to a large number not having brought their food,
six mills remained closed and six resumed work. It is expected that
Sunday, 1st March will see all at work on regular, both shifts.
About 65% of the night employees turned up, eleven of the mills
started work and one mill remained closed owing to the workers not
having brought their food.
    The Dong Shing Spinning & Weaving Mill, Gordon Road worked
all day and are working the night shift at full strength.
    Between 7 p.m. & 10 p.m. a meeting was held at the Labour
Union Headquarters, Chapel, between 300 and 400 strikers being pre-
sent, the majority from the Japan & China Cotton Mill, after heated
discussions about the promised strike pay the meeting broke up in
disorder.
    A further meeting has been called for Sunday afternoon,
March 1st 1925.
    Enquiries proceeding.
                                  I am, Sir,
                                   Yours obediently,
D.   C.                           D. S. Forbes

    该公司约60%的白班员工到岗，但由于许多人未携带食物，六家纱厂保持关闭，六家恢复工作。预计3月1日星期日，两班所有工人将正常上班。约65%的夜班员工到岗，十一家纱厂开工，一家纱厂因工人未带食物而保持关闭。

Sir:-
I beg to report that notwithstanding repeated applications
personally and by telephone to the Chinese Authorities (Chung Tsa
Ting) for the transfer to the Settlement of Sung Sheng Wei (孫良惠),
a strike agitator who was arrested in Chapei at the request of the

Ting on February 27th 1928 armed with the usual extradition documents
consisting of a Warrant and Despatch and requested that the prisoner
be handed over to the Settlement Authorities, pointing out the seri-
ousness of the offence against him. The application
The application was again refused, Magistrate Yuan stating
that a letter was sent to the Nanking Authorities three days ago in

number of strikers attempted to intimidate the Dong Shing female

the workers to make peace and return to work. They were all brought

由 D. S. Jordan 撰写。经 [签名] 转呈

先生：-

就普陀路地区棉纺厂罢工一事，谨此报告，所有 Bengal Wata Seisha Company（音译）的工厂目前仍处于关闭状态，但该厂宣布打算于1925年2月27日上午6时开放所有工厂复工。1925年2月26日，79%的日班员工和62%的夜班员工上交了工折，以便加盖印章领取50%的工资。

1925年2月26日上午6时，位于戈登路（Gordon Road）的东兴纱厂（Dong Shing Spinning & Weaving Mill）向工人开放，1038人（几乎满员）开始工作。他们全天工作，未出现任何骚乱迹象。夜班全员上岗，共有750名工人报到。

该地区部署了大量额外警力，采取了必要措施以保护工人。

没有出现恐吓迹象，无人被捕，该地区全天保持平静。据报，一些罢工者试图恐吓闸北（Chapei）的东兴女工，但工人们呼叫闸北巡捕协助，警方提供了援助，据悉当地并未发生逮捕事件。

1925年2月26日下午4时许，本捕房接到报告，称有一支举着白旗的队伍正沿澳门路（Macao Road）行进。

所有可用警力随即前往现场，发现一支约20名妇女组成的队伍，手持写有汉字的白旗，呼吁工人和解并返回工作岗位。她们全部被

to the Station for enquiries when it was learned that the leader of
the procession was a woman named Mon Tsu Ying (穆 志 英), chairman
of the Silk Filature Women Workers Union. She stated that she had
been invited down from Tsingkong a few days ago to assist in settling
the labour trouble and had received instructions from Sung Lien Fong
(宋 聯 芳) of the Chinese Chamber of Commerce to do her utmost to get
the people to return to work. She further stated that she had
received information that on February 24th 1925 the Labour Union had
received $50,000.00 from the Russian Communist agents in Shanghai to
prolong the strike, but she had not been able to verify that infor-
mation. After the necessary enquiries had been made, Inspector Foley
instructed that the flags be returned to the women to proceed with
the procession without interference.
        Between 7 a.m. and 10 a.m. February 26th 1925 a meeting
of twenty or thirty representatives of the strikers met at the
Labour Union Headquarters Chapel when they were told that they would
be held responsible for any of the strikers under their command
returning to work.
        At 5 p.m. a further meeting was held at their headquarters
about 300 or 400 people being present, during the course of the
meeting, it is reported that one of the Union officials, having the
appearance of a student, is alleged to have molested a Chinese female
where upon the strikers took the female's part and a fight of short
duration took part. The meeting then broke up without any police
interference.

        1925年2月26日上午7时至10时之间，二三十名罢工者代表在工会总部礼拜堂开会，会上被告知，若其管辖下的任何罢工者返回工作岗位，他们将对此承担责任。
        下午5时，在其总部再次举行会议，约有300至400人出席。据报，在会议过程中，一名看似学生的工会官员涉嫌骚扰一名中国女性，罢工者随即维护该女性，双方发生了短暂的斗殴。随后会议解散，警方未加干涉。

SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE.

REPORT OF POLICE INVESTIGATIONS.

The following is the statement of Foo Yuin Ting (傅雲汀), 26 years of age,
native of Pootung taken by me Detective Inspector Givers,
at Pootoo Rd. Stn on the 22nd Feb., 1925 and interpreted by Mr. Ben Sung.

My name is Foo Yuin Ting (傅雲汀). I am a native
of Pootung, and am employed in the Japan & China Cotton Mill. I
have been there for one year. I live in Tsa Ah Pang (草鞋浜) on
Gordon Road. While on the way home after finishing my work on
Wednesday ( February 17th, 1925 ) morning at 6 a.m., I met two
teachers of Puming Road Workers' School. The teachers in this
school changed frequently, and I do not know their names. All the
teachers came from the Shanghai University and Southern University.
The teachers were not paid a salary. Some of them however, who
were poor, were given ricksha fare from time to time. The money
for this purpose was taken from the society's funds, which were
raised by contributions of 10 cents each per month from the pupils.
Workers who used to visit the school for the purpose of recreation
paid the same as the pupils. When the teachers met me, they gave
me a bundle of pamphlets which they asked me to distribute. I was
arrested soon afterwards. I was formerly teacher of Japanese in
the school. I never saw any foreigners visit the school. Sung
Liang Wei (孫良惠) and Lieu Kwan Tseu (劉貫之) used to visit
the school frequently. Sung Liang Wei (孫良惠) was formerly a
police watchman. I saw him in uniform on Gordon Road.

This statement is made quite voluntary and is true.

(Sgd) Foo Yuin Ting.

以下为傅雲汀（Foo Yuin Ting），26岁，浦东人，于1925年2月22日在普陀路捕房由我，警探督察吉弗斯（Givers）警官录取，并由本松（Ben Sung）先生翻译的供词。

我叫傅雲汀（Foo Yuin Ting）。我是浦东人，受雇于日华纱厂（Japan & China Cotton Mill）。我在此工作已一年。我住在戈登路（Gordon Road）的草鞋浜（Tsa Ah Pang）。1925年2月17日（星期三）上午6点下班回家的路上，我遇到了两名普明路工人学校的教师。该校教师流动频繁，我不知道他们的姓名。所有教师均来自上海大学和南方大学。教师不领取薪水。然而，其中一些贫困的教师偶尔会获得黄包车车费补贴。这笔款项来自社团基金，由学生每月每人缴纳10分钱的捐款筹集而成。以前来学校娱乐的工人支付的费用与学生相同。当教师们遇到我时，他们给了我一捆小册子，让我分发。不久后我便被捕。我曾是该校的日语教师。我从未见过任何外国人访问该校。孙良惠（Sung Liang Wei）和刘贯之（Lieu Kwan Tseu）经常访问该校。孙良惠（Sung Liang Wei）曾是一名巡捕。我在戈登路见过他身穿制服。

本陈述完全出于自愿，且属实。

（签名）傅雲汀。

Pootoo Road Station.
February 26th, 1925.

Further REPORT ON Strike Situation.

Made by D. S. Forkin. Forwarded by J. McEig Inspector.

Sir:-

In connection with the strike situation in the Pootoo Road district, I beg to report that the Bengal Wata Kalena Company's Mills are still closed down, but about twenty or thirty men were employed in each of their mills cleaning machinery. This company paid out a bonus on February 25th, 1925, 80% of day workers receiving payment in the morning and 80% of night workers received payment in the evening. There is no information available as to when these mills will be opened to the workers.

The Dong Shing Spinning & Weaving Mill, Gordon Road will open their mill to the day workers on the morning of February 26th, 1925, notices have been posted to that effect.

Precautions have been taken by extra police on duty in the district against intimidators and disturbances of any kind.

Between 9 a.m. and 12 noon, and 1 p.m. and 4 p.m. February 25th 1925, about 20 representatives of the strikers met at the Labour Union Headquarters, Chapel, behind closed doors. They were instructed to inform the strikers that financial assistance had been promised by several Chinese cotton mills in the settlement and the Chapel Public Works Department, and that the strikers would receive the promised 20 cents daily during the strike, when the money was forthcoming. They were further instructed to urge to strikers to hold out for at least one week more and if by that time they had not received satisfaction, further action would be taken.

Enquiries proceeding.

I am, Sir,
Yours obediently,
J. Forkin
D. S.

Noted
D. McI X

关于罢工局势的补充报告。

由 D. S. Forkin 撰写。经 J. McEig 督察转呈。

先生：-

就普陀路地区的罢工局势，谨此报告，Bengal Wata Kalena Company（音译）的工厂仍处于关闭状态，但每家工厂雇佣了约二三十人清理机器。该公司于1925年2月25日发放了奖金，80%的日班工人在上午领到工资，80%的夜班工人在晚上领到工资。目前尚无关于这些工厂何时向工人开放的信息。

位于戈登路（Gordon Road）的东兴纱厂（Dong Shing Spinning & Weaving Mill）将于1925年2月26日上午向日班工人开放，已张贴相关通知。

该地区已部署额外警力，采取预防措施以防恐吓及任何形式的骚乱。

1925年2月25日上午9时至中午12时，以及下午1时至4时，约20名罢工者代表在工会总部礼拜堂闭门开会。他们受命告知罢工者，租界内的几家中国棉纺厂及礼拜堂工务局（Chapel Public Works Department，音译）已承诺提供财政援助，一旦资金到位，罢工者在罢工期间将获得承诺的每日20分钱。他们还受命敦促罢工者至少再坚持一周，如果届时仍未得到满意结果，将采取进一步行动。

调查正在进行中。

此致，
您顺从的仆人，
J. Forkin
D. S.

REPORT ON Arrest of persons charged with Intimidation in connection
with the cotton strike.

Made by D. S. Forkin. Forwarded by J. Foley Insp:

Sir:-

In connection with the present cotton strike, I beg to
report that at about 12 noon February 19th, 1925, with the assistance
of the Chapei Police, a man named Sung Liang Wei (孙良惠) was
arrested in Chapei charged with Intimidating the workers of the Naga
Wata Kaisha Company's Cotton Mills. A Mixed Court Warrant and a
Mixed Court Despatch Letter are on file at this Station for the
man's arrest. At 2.30 p.m. with the Despatch Letter a request was
made at the 4th Division Police Headquarters for him to be handed
over to us for trial before the International Mixed Court, but we
were referred to the Ching Tsa Ting (警察厅).

The application for extradition of this man will be held
over pending further instructions.

He is one of the leaders of the strike movement, has been
the chief spokesman at the meetings in Chapei and has represented
himself as the chief representative of the Nanking University,
whereas, he is unemployed, an ex-police watchman, and a resident of
the International Settlement.

At 10.15 a.m. February 19th, 1925 a man named Zang Yen Sung
(盛逸生) was arrested at Tongquin Road and charged with Intimidating
the workers of the Dong Shing Cotton Mill. He is a coolie employed
at the Dong Shing Mill, residing at No. 6 Macao Road and is known to
have taken a prominent part in the present strike. When searched he
had in his possession a letter chopped "Labour Union of Dong Shing
Cotton Mill" inviting the strikers to a meeting at a teashop in Cha-
pei and which he stated he had received that morning from their
Headquarters with instructions to show it to the people concerned.

Translation of an anonymous letter.

Inspector:-
I beg to report on the strike situation of the Naiga
Wata Kaisha Cotton Mills.
A famous loafer named Zao Hai Ching who has provoked
the workers of the Naiga Wata Kaisha Cotton Mills to strike has his
Headquarters in the Dong Shing Mill Quarters, No. 92 Macao Road.
The said house is occupied by Zao where evidence will be found con-
cerning the present strike. Before the strike Zao gathered a number
of workers to a meeting at his quarters with the result that all the
workers of the Naiga Wata Kaisha Cotton Mills struck work & damaged
a great deal of property. On the 11th inst. Zao held a meeting tel-
ling the people that the Japan & China Cotton Mill was also Japanese
& that he should be assaulted & the factory destroyed. All the work-
ers were fooled by him & damaged the said mill, I don't know the
value, all the workers struck their work. On the 15th inst. he held
another meeting saying that the Dong Shing Cotton Mill was Japanese
& that it should be destroyed in a few days, therefore Zao is a man
who has committed riot in the Settlement.
At a certain meeting Zao said that if the Japanese do
not give way to us we must unite together.
If the Police assist the Japanese in arresting us, then
we can unite together & attack the Police on a certain day as we have
more than 10,000 workers.
We must set fire to various places so that the Police
will not have time to extinguish them. We have been ill-treated by
the Japanese and the Police also attempt to ill-treat us, therefore
we must attack them with our lives. I have investigated & find that
Zao is a very bad man against your Settlement. I live in the Settle-
ment & must report you the above facts, therefore I hope you will
immediately search his house whether he has strike evidence or not.
I think you must immediately investigate otherwise it will be too late.
pages.zh:
匿名信译文。

督察：

谨就内家棉纺织株式会社（Naiga Wata Kaisha）棉纺厂的罢工局势报告如下。
一个叫趙海清的著名无赖，煽动内家棉纺织株式会社棉纺厂工人罢工，其据点位于澳门路92号的东兴纱厂宿舍。
該住所由趙占用，其中可找到有关当前罢工的证据。罢工前，趙在其住所召集工人开会，导致内家棉纺织株式会社棉纺厂所有工人罢工并损坏了大量财产。本月11日，趙召开会议，声称日华棉纺厂也是日本人的，应当受到攻击，工厂应当被摧毁。所有工人都被他愚弄，损坏了该厂，损失价值我不清楚，所有工人都停止了工作。本月15日，他又召开一次会议，称东兴棉纺厂是日本人的，应当在几天内被摧毁，因此趙是一个在租界内犯有暴动罪的人。
在一次会议上，趙说如果日本人不向我们让步，我们必须团结起来。
如果警察协助日本人逮捕我们，那么我们可以团结起来，在某一天攻击警察，因为我们有超过一万名工人。
我们必须四处放火，使警察无暇灭火。我们受到日本人的虐待，警察也试图虐待我们，因此我们必须以死相拼。经我调查，發現趙是一个对贵租界非常有害的人。我住在租界内，必须向您报告上述事实，因此希望您立即搜查他的住所，看他是否藏有罢工证据。
我认为您必须立即调查，否则为时已晚。

现已知悉，当前骚乱的支持者是俄国共产主义者。据说，作为俄国共产主义机构且受加拉罕（Karakhan）控制的大夏大学（Dah Ito College），已向煽动者提供资金以支付其开销。

上海棉纺厂联合会致电外交部部长。

显然，当前骚乱中的煽动者是俄国共产主义者的代理人。俄国无视最近刚刚恢复的日俄友谊，这是一件严重的事情。我们真诚希望我国政府与相关的俄国方面进行谈判，制止骚乱。

Translation of Chinese Pamphlet.
6026
18/2/25

Brothers & Sisters! The Manager of our mills is also a Japanese
who ill-treated us the same as the Naiga Wata Kaisha mill workers were &
who dismissed the workers & gave the remainder extra work.
It is very dangerous for the workers to lose their business. The
workers who remain in the mills have been given extra work, therefore, we
struck work yesterday morning & ask the following seven demands.
1. Can not reduce the staff & do not dismiss any workers without
reasons.
2. Hereafter the worker must not be assaulted.
3. The workers will not be fined in future.
4. The dismissal of Tsong Yah (Japanese) & he must not be em-
ployed again.
5. An increase of 1/10 in wages.
6. If a worker resigns, his wages will not be forfeited.
7. The mill management must pay attention to health conditions.
These are our inferior demands.
Now we take an oath to unite with the Naiga Wata Kaisha mill
workers & utterly refuse to return to work unless we conquer.
We earnestly hope that all brothers & sisters will come out to
assist us in order to attack the Japanese to get a final win.

All workers in Nos. 1 & 2 of Dah Koang
Cotton Mills.
pages.zh:
中文传单译文。
6026
1925年2月18日

兄弟姐妹们！我们工厂的经理也是日本人，他像对待内外棉株式会社工厂工人一样虐待我们，解雇了工人，并给留下的人增加了额外的工作。
工人失业是非常危险的。留在工厂的工人被增加了额外的工作，因此，我们昨天早上罢工，并提出以下七项要求。
1. 不得减少员工，不得无故解雇任何工人。
2. 今后不得殴打工人。
3. 今后不得罚款工人。
4. 解雇宗亚（Tsong Yah，音译，日本人），且不得再雇用他。
5. 工资增加十分之一。
6. 如果工人辞职，其工资不会被没收。
7. 工厂管理层必须注意健康状况。
这些是我们卑微的要求。
现在我们发誓与内外棉株式会社工厂工人团结在一起，除非取得胜利，否则坚决拒绝复工。
我们恳切希望所有兄弟姐妹出来协助我们，以便攻击日本人并取得最终胜利。

大广棉厂（Dah Koang Cotton Mills，音译）1号和2号全体工人。

REPORT ON Stoppage of work at the Dong Shing Cotton Mill,
Gordon Rd.

Made by D.S. Forkin Forwarded by J. Molyneux Inspector

Sir,

I beg to report that at 1.40 a.m., February 16th., 1925,
message
a telephone was received from the Dong Shing cotton mill,
Gordon Rd. reporting that one of their departments had struck
work. Enquiries were immediately made when it was
ascertained from Mr. Kishimoto, the manager, that at 1.30 a.m.
the hands in the fly spinning dept., numbering about 100
(70 men and 30 women) stopped work but remained in the mill.

A half hearted attempt appears to have been made by one or
two coolies to get the remainder to strike and damage the mill
as several windows were broken with bars and bobbins and four
frames put out of working order. On the arrival of the police
all the male workers were in the dining room with the females at
their frames. After a lot of persuasion with a promise
that no action would be taken should they all return to work,
they all resumed at 2.45 a.m..

There are 780 night workers at this mill and every other
dept. carried on with their work the whole night.

A police guard is being kept on the mill as it is probable
that another attempt will be made to get the workers to strike.

Enquiries proceeding.

I am, Sir,
Yours obediently,
J. Forkin
D.S.

D.C.I.

电话
接到戈登路同兴纱厂来电，报告该厂某一部门已罢工。立即进行调查，从经理岸本先生（Mr. Kishimoto）处获悉，凌晨1时30分，粗纱部约100名工人（70名男工和30名女工）停止工作，但仍留在厂内。

似乎有一两名苦力半心半意地试图让其余工人罢工并破坏工厂，因为有几扇窗户被铁条和纱管打破，四台机器被弄坏无法运转。警察到达时，所有男工均在餐厅，女工则在各自的机器旁。经过大量劝说，并承诺若所有人复工将不采取任何行动后，他们于凌晨2时45分全部恢复工作。

该厂有780名夜班工人，其他所有部门整夜均正常工作。

警方正在对该厂进行守卫，因为很可能再次有人试图煽动工人罢工。

调查正在进行中。

先生，

14/2/25

Friendly workers!

At present there are some rumours coming from the mills
stating that on both Sides of the Creek arrests are being made. but you must
not believe them. There is no one to arrest any workers if we unite. Now
there is a law which is called The Labour Union Act and it states that a
Strike is not unlawful. Nobody can arrest us. The nine workers arrest-
ed by the Police will be immediately released on intervention of the Union.
They dare not detain them. Again a rumour states that the Mills will be
closed and there is an announcement posted at the doorway for that purpose,
but you will understand that it is absolutely false in order to bluff us.
The Japanese love money as they do their lives, so they will not close the
mills on that account, as they must lose a lot of their capital. Friendly
workers! If we unite together in this Strike the Japanese will fear the
loss of their capital and so must consent to our demands. The Union is
our representative; & the regulations, you should obey. Our Union is
situated at Sai Tuh Lee (三德里) behind the Dah Foong Cotton Mill (大豐紗廠),
North of the Creek. You can get news either from the Union or the Union
will tell you.

(Chopped) Labour Union of Naiga Wata
Kaisha Cotton Mills.

1925年2月14日

各位工友！

目前厂方散布谣言，称小河两岸正在抓人。但切勿相信。只要我们团结，无人敢逮捕任何工人。现有一部法律名为《工会法》，规定罢工并非违法。无人能逮捕我们。被警察逮捕的九名工人，经工会干预后将立即获释。他们不敢扣留这些人。另有谣言称工厂将关闭，并在门口张贴告示以此为目的，但你们应明白这完全是为了吓唬我们的虚假宣传。日本人爱财如命，因此不会因此关闭工厂，否则他们将损失大量资本。各位工友！如果我们在此次罢工中团结一致，日本人将因害怕资本损失而不得不答应我们的要求。工会是我们的代表；规章条例，你们应当遵守。我们的工会位于大豐紗廠后方、小河北侧的三德里（Sai Tuh Lee）。你们可以从工会获取消息，或者工会也会告知你们。

（盖章）内外棉株式会社纱厂工会。

Further REPORT ON Strike Situation.

Made by D.S. Andrews.         Forwarded by H. Hodging [signature]

Sir:-

    I beg to report that the Situation around the different
mills effected by the Strike at No. 5 Mill remains about the
same as last evening February 10th, 1925.

    Nos. 5, 7, 8, 9 & 12 Mills were not opened to workers,
although a number of mill hands turned up at the usual time.

    About 100 hands turned up belonging to Nos. 13 & 14 Mills
but after working for an hour or so they requested to leave.

    Nos. 3 & 4 Mills were filled at 6 a.m. today & remained
till about 5.30 p.m. when they left for their homes, as some of
the hands failed to bring food. These two mills are working to-
night but are short of about 200.

    A Demonstration of about 300 men was held on the Chapei
Side of Soochow Creek opposite Nos. 3 & 4 Mills the object being
to intimidate workers who had to cross the Creek to these mills.

    One man who had the appearance of a student was obviously
inciting the crowd.

    Three men were arrested off Ferry Road trying to prevent
workers from proceeding to work. One of these men when question-
ed stated he had received a badge from students after attending
a meeting at 9 a.m. February 11th, 1925 behind the Dan Foong
Cotton Mill ( 大 豐 紗 廠 ), Chapei. There are about 20 stu-
dents holding meeting at this place each day since the Strike.

    Further enquiries are being made as to the source of the
trouble which undoubtedly started at No. 5 Mill, & will be repor-
ted on.

                                I am Sir,
D. C. I.                        Yours obediently,
                                H. Hodging [signature]

REPORT ON Further Report on Strike at No. 9 Mill.

Made by D.S. Andrews. Forwarded by [Signature]

Sir:-

I beg to report that at 10.45 a.m. February 10th, 1925 a message was received from Mr. Motoki Assistant Manager of the Naiga Wata Kaisha Cotton Mills, reporting trouble at No. 9 Mill Markham Road.

Accompanied by S/I Adams, Sergeant Hendery & Chinese Detectives I proceeded to the Mill immediately.

On arrival we observed a large number of workers outside & also a large number having quiet orderly. When we got inside the Main Gates a crowd of men were seen in a very excited manner coming from the direction of the offices. A number of these men attacked us & made good their escape outside the Mill amongst the crowd. One man was arrested.

From enquiries it was ascertained that about 200 men on Strike from No. 5 Mill had proceeded to No. 9 Mill Markham Road where they entered, in the hopes of getting the workers numbering about 1,500 to join them.

Some of the strikers proceeded to the offices & smashed all the windows & interior fittings assaulting several Japanese employers.

Another party made their way to the Carding & Spinning rooms where the mill employees were peacefully working, & started to break electric fittings, delicate parts of motors & some of the machinery- the damage done is not estimated at a large sum but sufficient to stop work at this mill for a few days.

The mill workers all left after trouble with the strikers but it was perfectly obvious, they were not in sympathy.

In the meantime we received information that the strikers

关于第九厂罢工的进一步报告。

由 D.S. Andrews 制作。由 [签名] 转呈

先生：

谨此报告，1925年2月10日上午10时45分，收到内外棉株式会社纱厂副经理 Motoki 先生的消息，报告马克姆路（Markham Road）第九厂发生骚乱。

我在副督察 Adams、警长 Hendery 及华籍侦探的陪同下，立即前往该厂。

抵达时，我们观察到厂外有大量工人，另有许多人保持安静有序。当我们进入大门内时，看到一群人从办公室方向非常激动地涌来。其中一些人袭击了我们，并混入厂外人群中成功逃脱。一人被捕。

经查询得知，约200名来自第五厂的罢工者前往马克姆路第九厂并进入厂内，希望争取约1500名工人加入他们。

一些罢工者前往办公室，砸碎所有窗户和内部设施，并袭击了几名日本雇主。

另一伙人闯入清花间和纺纱间，当时厂方员工正在平静工作，他们开始破坏电气装置、电机的精密部件以及一些机器——造成的损失金额估计不大，但足以使该厂停工数日。

在与罢工者发生冲突后，厂方工人全部离开，但显而易见，他们并不同情罢工者。

与此同时，我们收到消息，罢工者

正前往其他日本纱厂。已向普陀路分局发出电话警告，但罢工者在警察到达之前已抵达罗宾森路（Robinson Road）第十三及十四厂，部分人得以强行进入厂内。他们采取了与第九厂相同的手段——砸毁办公室并闯入机器车间，但由于普陀路分局的援助及时赶到，造成的损失很小。冲突中有数名日本人遭到袭击。

十一人在第十三及十四厂内及周边地区被捕，连同在第九厂逮捕的一人，将于明天即1925年2月11日以煽动暴乱罪在会审公廨被起诉。

在第十三及十四厂的罢工者被驱散后，看来他们穿过苏州河进入闸北，直到下午4时30分左右，该地区一切平静，未见进一步骚乱迹象。在上述时间，有人看到这批人在斐伦路（Ferry Road）码头附近的苏州河北岸聚集，以阻止工人渡河前往第三及四厂（白天这些工厂未发生骚乱）。

他们的这一方法相当成功，因为 Okada 先生向我报告，晚上6点只有约100名工人前来上夜班，因此他决定停止夜班工作。

第十三及十四厂的夜班工人按惯例出勤，但由于预计会与罢工者发生更多麻烦，他们请求允许回家。

苏州河西路的第5、7、8及12号纱厂均已停工，原因是日方职员工作量增加，冈田先生（Mr. Okada）认为最好让他们休息一下。
第9号纱厂已关闭，直至受损机器修复为止，并在正门张贴了相关告示。
位于普陀路分局对面的第15号纱厂，是目前内海棉业株式会社（Naiga Wata Kaisha Company）旗下唯一实际开工的纱厂。该厂未发生任何麻烦。
冈田先生明确表示，他的公司愿尽一切努力允许工人进厂工作，但由于罢工者的存在，这在大多数情况下已不可能；此外，公司完全愿意与工人认可的任何代表团体会面，以听取任何正当的诉求，但既然工人诉诸暴力，他表示别无选择，只能关闭纱厂，直到工人愿意在现有条件下返工为止。
冈田先生向我指出，内海棉业株式会社旗下的纱厂工人获得的薪酬及个人生活设施条件，优于在华资公司工作的待遇。
平均每位纱厂工人每日获得50.7分的生活津贴（原文：pig living money，疑为笔误），免费医疗——无罚款——以及以大幅降低的租金居住公司自有住房的便利。

REPORT ON Strike at No. 5 Mill.

Made by D.S. Andrews. Forwarded by J. Holly Inspr.

Sir:-
I beg to report that at 3.55 p.m., February 9th, 1925 a Telephone Message was received from Mr. S. Okada, manager of the Naiga Wata Kaisha Cotton Mills reporting a strike at No. 5 Mill situated on West Soocnow Road.

Accompanied by native detectives I proceeded to the scene & was informed by the Supt. Mr. Kawamara that about 1,500 workers employed in the Speeding_Card, and Ring rooms situated on the East side of No. 5 Mill were on strike & trying to intimidate other workers in Nos. 7, 8, and 12 Mills, but they were prevented & eventually got out side the mill without causing any serious damage to machinery etc.

Information was first received on Sunday, February 8th, 1925 by Supt. Taji of No. 5 Mill, who was in Charge at this time, the Mill being closed down on Sunday & only leaving a small number of workmen to look after the machinery. Mr. Taji heard from these workers that a general strike was anticipated on the 9th February, 1925. Steps were immediately taken by him to prevent it, by calling all representatives of the workers together, but owing to the mill being closed it was only possible to get a small number which proved ineffective.

Today, enquiries were made & it was reported by Mr. S. Okada that every thing was quiet & orderly no further news of a strike pending.

About noon pamphlets were distributed amongst the workers, a copy of which is attached, with a translation, and at 3 p.m. the workers in the different rooms mentioned above on the East wing of

Translation of Chinese pamphlet.

Friends of Nan Yan Cotton Mill.

We are extremely bitter when we work in the Japanese
Cotton Mill and we, daily, work over twelve hours. The wages that we
earn are so small. If any one is found bad, the Japanese will assault
this man with clenched fists and kick him with his feet. If any small
mistake has been done, he will be fined. The Japanese treat us,
workers, same as oxen or ponies. The Japanese fine or assault us as
he likes and he has no idea to talk the health or principal between us.
The 2nd inst. of this current month the manager of the No. 8 Mill had
dismissed all the workers who worked in the rough cotton department.
On the 4th inst. of this month the ex-workers went to the mentioned Mill
to ask for wages. The Japanese not only refused to pay the wages but
arrested their representatives sending them to the Police Station to be
charged. Oh! Workers! the Japanese treat us same as animals. The Japanese
not only drink our blood and deprive our skin from our bodies. There is
no reason for this treatment. Friends! the Japanese compel us to have no
path to proceed, so we hope to strike in order to oppose the bad treatment
and also apply the following articles.

1. Hereafter no assault.
2. One tenth rate promotion to the original wages.
3. To resume the work among the workers who had been dismissed from
No. 8 Mill and also have the workers to be released at once who
have been charged.
4. To give wages one time in two weeks with no delay.
5. The mill must pay us the wages during the strike time.
6. From hereafter, to dismiss any worker must have some proper reason.

Friends! Workers! if the mill recognizes the above
articles then we can have a life. We must hold our strike till the good
result.

Workers in the Nan Yan Cotton Mill.

中文小册子译文。

南炎纱厂的朋友们。

我们在日本纱厂工作极其痛苦，我们每天工作超过十二小时。我们挣得的工资微薄。如果有人表现不好，日本人就会用拳头殴打此人，并用脚踢他。如果犯了一点小错，就会被罚款。日本人对待我们工人如同牛马。日本人随意罚款或殴打我们，根本不顾及我们的健康或原则。
本月2日，第8号纱厂经理解雇了所有在粗棉部工作的工人。
本月4日，被解雇的工人前往上述纱厂索要工资。日本人不仅拒绝支付工资，还逮捕了他们的代表，将他们送往警察局控告。哦！工人们！日本人把我们当作动物一样对待。日本人不仅吸我们的血，剥我们的皮。这种对待毫无道理。朋友们！日本人逼得我们走投无路，所以我们希望罢工以反对恶劣待遇，并提出以下条款。

1. 今后不得殴打。
2. 在原工资基础上增加十分之一。
3. 恢复第8号纱厂被解雇工人的工作，并立即释放被控告的工人。
4. 每两周发一次工资，不得拖延。
5. 罢工期间，纱厂必须支付我们工资。
6. 今后，解雇任何工人必须有正当理由。

朋友们！工人们！如果纱厂承认上述条款，我们才能生存。我们必须坚持罢工，直到取得良好结果。

南炎纱厂工人。

Translation of Chinese Pamphlet.

Male and Female friendly workers!
We are now compelled going to strike on account of us being ill-treated, assaulted and scolded by the Japanese. Also the Japanese dismissed our workers, deduct our wages without reasons and frequently delay to pay our wages.
Not only we have performed the strike and the eleven mills are all on strike. 20000workers unite in one heart and ought to put one's life on it in order to determine whether you and we take the death or not.
We strike and win then what are the benefits for us?
1. The Japanese dare not to assault us again.
2. Increase our wages with one tentn, e.g. fifteen dollars may increase one dollar and half, ten dollars to eleven etc.
3. The wages within the strike period will be paid us originally.
4. Afterwards the wages must be paid one time in two weeks without delay.
5. To have the workers who have been charged to be released at once.
In one word there are many benefits so that we are boldly doing on not afraid.
How we can get favour?
1. We, 20000workers, want to unite to do together then not afraid the Japanese will not permit us.
2. We should under the direction of labour union. The labour union is the defence body which protect us. We are hearing the union order whether going to work or not.
We never fail if we all obey the union order.
Friendly workers! that is union words which say to you good, you may keep them in your mind always and not forget. The favour is ours.

中文小册子译文。

男女工友们！
我们现在被迫罢工，因为我们受到日本人的虐待、殴打和辱骂。此外，日本人无故解雇我们的工人，克扣我们的工资，并经常拖欠工资。
我们不仅举行了罢工，而且十一家纱厂全部罢工。20,000名工人同心协力，应当豁出性命，以决定你我是否赴死。
如果我们罢工获胜，对我们有什么好处？
1. 日本人不敢再殴打我们。
2. 增加我们十分之一的工资，例如十五元可增加一元五角，十元增至十一元等。
3. 罢工期间的工资将照常支付给我们。
4. 此后工资必须每两周发放一次，不得拖延。
5. 立即释放被控告的工人。
总之好处多多，所以我们大胆行动，无所畏惧。
我们如何能获得利益？
1. 我们20,000名工人要团结一起行动，就不怕日本人不允许。
2. 我们应在工会的指导下行动。工会是保护我们的防御组织。我们听从工会命令决定是否上班。
如果我们都服从工会命令，就绝不会失败。
工友们！这是工会对你们说的良言，你们应牢记在心，切勿忘记。利益属于我们。

REPORT ON Mixed Court proceedings against strikers.

Made by P. Tizon, Clerical Asst. Forwarded by [Signature]

Sir,

At the Mixed Court at 2 p.m. to-day, before Mr. Tajima, Japanese Assessor, and magistrate Loh, 陸 Wang Ah Nyi 王阿二 15, mill hand, Soong Ang Kwei 宋安桂 17, mill hand, Tsoong Pao Kong 鐘宝庫 23, mill hand, Koh Yoong Sing 高士林 22, shop assistant, Wong Yoong Chong 王永昌 18, mill hand, Tsoong Hung Fah 陈仁发 21, mill hand, Koh Zung Ching 高仁進 19, mill hand, Yi Yui Pao 嚴余波 23, mill hand, and Sih Wen Soong 謝懷松 22, mill hand (who is sick in hospital) appeared on the following charges:-

1) For that they on the 15th day of February at No. 200 Jessfield Road at the cotton mill there situate did assemble for the purpose of committing violence and being there and then assembled together were guilty of riotous behaviour, contrary to Article 164 of the Chinese Provisional Criminal Code,

2) For that they at the same time and place concerned together with others not yet in custody did maliciously damage certain property, to wit, mill machinery the property of the complainant, the Toyoda Cotton Mill, contrary to Article 405 of the Chinese Provisional Criminal Code.

Mr. A. T. Maitland, Prosecuting Solicitor, appeared for the Police; Mr. A. Covey for the defence.

Mr. Maitland: These men are charged with riotous behaviour and with doing malicious damage at the Toyoda Cotton Mill.

Det. Sergt. Macgregor, called, said: I arrested the 2nd, 5th, 6th, 7th and 8th accused in the Toyoda Cotton Mill for doing malicious damage in the carding room. They were breaking up the machinery. The 3rd and the 4th accused were arrested on Jessfield Road outside the mill. The 1st accused was arrested by a Japanese overseer at the mill for breaking up the electric light. At 4 p.m. on February 14 a telephone message was received from the Toyoda mill at Bubbling Well Road Station that there were rumours current that the Chinese employees were going on strike. At 6.30 p.m. another telephone message was received stating that the men had come out on strike and were breaking up the machinery. Accompanied by two foreign constables I went to the mill and found about 1,000 employees outside the gate of the mill on Jessfield Road. I forced my way through the crowd into the mill when one of the Japanese overseers had arrested one of the accused for breaking an electric globe. Accompanied by one of the constables I went to the carding room and there found the 2nd, the 5th, the 6th, the 7th and the 8th accused breaking up the machinery. We placed them under arrest and took them to the

先生：

今日下午2时，在会审公廨，于日本陪审员田岛先生（Mr. Tajima）及罗法官面前，以下人员就下列指控出庭：王阿二（Wang Ah Nyi），15岁，工厂工人；宋安桂（Soong Ang Kwei），17岁，工厂工人；鐘宝庫（Tsoong Pao Kong），23岁，工厂工人；高士林（Koh Yoong Sing），22岁，店员；王永昌（Wong Yoong Chong），18岁，工厂工人；陈仁发（Tsoong Hung Fah），21岁，工厂工人；高仁進（Koh Zung Ching），19岁，工厂工人；嚴余波（Yi Yui Pao），23岁，工厂工人；以及謝懷松（Sih Wen Soong），22岁，工厂工人（因病住院）。指控如下：

1) 指控他们于2月15日在杰斯菲尔德路（Jessfield Road）200号的棉纺厂内聚集，意图实施暴力，且当时聚集在一起，犯有扰乱治安行为，违反《中华民国暂行新刑律》第164条，

2) 指控他们在同一时间、同一地点，与其他尚未被捕之人共谋，恶意损坏某些财产，即原告丰田棉纺厂（Toyoda Cotton Mill）的工厂机械，违反《中华民国暂行新刑律》第405条。

公诉律师 A. T. Maitland 先生代表警方出庭；A. Covey 先生代表辩方。

Maitland 先生：这些人被控在丰田棉纺厂犯有扰乱治安罪及恶意破坏罪。

传召警长 Macgregor 作证，他说：我在丰田棉纺厂的梳棉间逮捕了第2、第5、第6、第7和第8名被告，因为他们正在那里进行恶意破坏。他们正在拆毁机器。第3和第4名被告是在厂外杰斯菲尔德路上被捕的。第1名被告因拆毁电灯，被厂内一名日本监工逮捕。2月14日下午4时，静安寺路分局接到来自丰田纱厂的电话消息，称有谣言流传，中国雇员即将罢工。下午6时30分，又接到另一通电话，称工人已罢工并正在拆毁机器。我随同两名外籍巡捕前往该厂，发现约有1000名雇员聚集在杰斯菲尔德路的厂门外。我强行穿过人群进入厂内，当时一名日本监工已因一名被告打破电灯泡而将其逮捕。我随同其中一名巡捕前往梳棉间，发现第2、第5、第6、第7和第8名被告正在拆毁机器。我们将他们逮捕并带至

gate of the mill. A crowd of workers had got out of the mill by that time, and were throwing stones breaking the windows, creating a disturbance and rioting. The doors of the mill were closed and the Police retired into the mill. After a time it quietened down. I went out on the road and arrested the 3rd and 4th accused who were in the midst of a crowd of about 200, the remainder having dispersed. The motor car from Bubbling Well Station was on Jessfield Road and the strikers pushed the car into the Soochow Creek. About this time, a number of Japanese employees drove up to the mill in a motor car. The strikers stopped the car, pulled them out and assaulted them. One man was shot with a .32 revolver through the right side by one of the strikers; another Japanese was struck over the head with a blunt instrument and then thrown into the Soochow Creek. He was later rescued by boatmen and sent to hospital where he has since died.
Mr. Covey (cross-examining): When you arrived were there not three sections of strikers in front of the place?
Witness: No.
Counsel: How many sections were there?
Witness: I don't quite understand you.
Counsel: At the entrance to the mill, you would say there were how many strikers?
Witness: About 1,000. The night shift was coming off and the day shift was going on. There were men and women.
Counsel: And when you came out of the mill there were how many?
Witness: 250. The others had dispersed.
Counsel: 250 were on Jessfield Road?
Witness: Yes.
Counsel: At what time did you make the arrests?
Witness: 7.30.
Counsel: It was probably dark?
Witness: Yes.
Mr. Covey here informed the Court that he would deal with the 9th accused, who was in hospital, at the same time.
Mr. Covey (to witness): The 2nd, the 5th, the 6th, the 7th, the 8th and the 9th accused were arrested in the carding room?
Witness: Yes.
Counsel: And I take it that the whole of the mill was in darkness when you arrived?
Witness: No.
Counsel: What part was in darkness?
Witness: The carding room.
Counsel: Were the lights put on again?
Witness: The lights were put on inside of ten minutes.
Counsel: A dim light?
Witness: Yes.
Counsel: Did you know that all these men were waiting until the lights were put on?
Witness: No.

厂门口。此时，一群工人已从厂内出来，他们投掷石块砸碎窗户，制造骚乱和暴动。工厂大门关闭，警察退入厂内。过了一段时间，局势平息。我走到路上，逮捕了混在约200人人群中的第3和第4名被告，其余人已散去。静安寺分局的汽车停在杰斯菲尔德路上，罢工者将车推入苏州河。大约在此时，数名日本雇员乘汽车抵达工厂。罢工者拦住汽车，将他们拉出并殴打。其中一名日本人被一名罢工者用一把.32口径左轮手枪击中右侧身体；另一名日本人头部被钝器击打，随后被抛入苏州河。他后来被船夫救起并送往医院，后在医院死亡。
Covey 先生（交叉询问）：当你到达时，现场前面不是有三批罢工者吗？
证人：不。
律师：有几批？
证人：我不太明白你的意思。
律师：在工厂入口处，你说有多少罢工者？
证人：大约1000人。夜班下班，白班上班。其中有男有女。
律师：当你从工厂出来时，有多少人？
证人：250人。其他人已散去。
律师：250人在杰斯菲尔德路上？
证人：是的。
律师：你是什么时候逮捕他们的？
证人：7点30分。
律师：当时天可能黑了吧？
证人：是的。
Covey 先生此时告知法庭，他将同时处理目前在医院的第9名被告的案件。
Covey 先生（问证人）：第2、第5、第6、第7、第8和第9名被告是在梳棉间被捕的？
证人：是的。
律师：我想请问，当你到达时，整个工厂都陷入黑暗了吗？
证人：不。
律师：哪部分处于黑暗中？
证人：梳棉间。
律师：灯后来又亮了吗？
证人：十分钟内灯就亮了。
律师：光线昏暗？
证人：是的。
律师：你是否知道这些人都在等待灯光亮起？
证人：不。

Counsel: You did not know that?
Witness: No.
Counsel: Comparing the attitude of these men (pointing to the dock) and the attitude of the 250, which was the worse?
Witness: I am not here to judge them on their attitude.
Counsel: You arrested them for malicious damage?
Witness: For sabotage.
Counsel: You spoke of their attitude in your examination-in-chief.
Witness: I spoke of the 250.
Counsel: In your opinion which, would you say, were the worse: the 250 or the boys in the dock now?
Witness: I am not prepared to go into the question.
Counsel: You referred to Japanese driving up in a motor car and being assaulted, and also of one Japanese being shot and of another being thrown into a creek by the strikers. Are any of these men in Court?
Witness: No.
Mr. Maitland: I can call other witnesses who will only say the same thing if the Court wishes.
The Assessor: Have you any more questions to ask the witness, Mr. Covey?
Mr. Covey: No, Sir. With the exception of the 4th accused, whom I do not represent in this case, I simply throw myself on the mercy of the Court.
The Assessor: You said the 2nd, the 5th, the 6th, the 7th, the 8th, and the 9th accused were wrecking the machinery in the carding room?
Witness: Yes.
The Assessor: With what?
Witness: They had iron bars.
The Assessor: Were these iron bars seized?
Witness: They were left in the mill. They are attached to the machines. The damage done was very slight. The 3rd and 4th accused were arrested outside the mill. They were throwing stones at windows breaking them.
The Assessor: Did they have anything else in their hands?
Witness: Yes, some of them had sticks.
The Assessor: Are all the accused mill hands?
Witness: All except one who is an assistant in a bean shop. This is the 4th accused.

Dr. O. Fischer, who is appearing for the 4th accused, cross-examining: Did you see the stones the 4th accused threw?
Witness: Yes.
Counsel: How big?
Witness: About the size of my fist.
Counsel: Have you the stones here?
Witness: No, if they had been all brought to the Station they would have made a huge heap.

Counsel: The 4th accused is not an employee in the cotton
mill; what motive can he have in throwing stones?
Witness: It can be proved that it was not the mill hands who
desired the strike, it was the agitators.
Counsel: In your opinion, does the 4th accused have the
appearance of an agitator?
Witness: Yes.
Counsel: Do you know where he is employed?
Witness: In the village near the mill. I verified that.
Counsel: Did you personally arrest him?
Witness: Yes.
Counsel: Did you ask him any questions?
Witness: Yes. He said he was employed in a bean shop. I
verified that also.
Counsel: Did he tell you how it happened that he was there?
Witness: He said he was on his way home.
Counsel: Did he deny having anything to do with the strike?
Witness: He did not deny it. I asked him why he had the
stones in his hands. He said he was not in any way connected
with the strike.

All the accused were then examined by the Magistrate, with
the exception of the 4th accused whose examination-in-chief was
led by his Counsel, Dr. Fischer.
The questions and replies were not interpreted into English,
except in the case of the 4th accused, who said: My name is Koh
Ying Sing. I am employed in a bean shop not far from the mill.
When passing the mill, I was arrested by foreign detectives.
Dr. Fischer: Did you hear the evidence of the foreign
detective who said you had stones in your hands?
Accused: I was passing there and did not throw any stones.
I did not ask anyone about the strike. I don't know anybody.
In answer to the Magistrate, accused said: I was simply
walking and passed the mill. I did not stand near the mill. I
did not see any stones thrown.
The Magistrate: How many people were there?
Accused: I don't know.
The Magistrate: But you were passing there, so you must
know?
Accused: I don't know.
The Assessor: You must know. There were about 200 together.
The Magistrate: When you were arrested did you see anyone
throwing stones?
Accused: I don't know.
The Assessor (lifting up one of his hands): Can you see this?
Accused: I don't know. (Laughter).
The Assessor (questioning Det. Sergt. Macgregor): When you
arrested the 3rd and 4th accused, had the motor car containing

随后，除第4名被告由其辩护律师 Fischer 医生主导主询问外，所有被告均接受法官讯问。
除第4名被告的情况外，问答内容未翻译成英文，第4名被告说：我叫 Koh Ying Sing（音译）。我在离工厂不远的一家豆行工作。路过工厂时，我被外籍侦探逮捕。

法官：那里有多少人？
被告：我不知道。
法官：但你经过那里，所以你应该知道吧？
被告：我不知道。
陪审员：你应该知道。当时大约有200人聚在一起。
法官：你被捕时，看到有人扔石块吗？
被告：我不知道。

被告：我不知道。（笑声）。

One for
Sir,
With reference to the labour unrest in the District, I beg
to forward the following information re. memo. dated 26th February
1925.
(1). There is no information to show that the strikers were mem-
-bers of any particular union or that they foregathered in any place
in the District. Information was received regarding the strike at
the Toyoda Cotton Mill on February 14, 1925 that a girl student
was active in the mill before they came out. Who the student was
or what school she came from cannot be ascertained.
(2). The origin of the dispute can be attributed to agitation
by mill workers from the Japanese mills in Gordon Road District.
(3). With reference to the Shanghai Leather Co. strike discon-
tent intimidation was the cause. There was no apparent discontent among
the worker of the Toyoda and owing to a general lock out being
declared there was very little intimidation.

in the District.

and Light School are believed to have taken an active part
in promoting the strike.

198
关于静安寺区劳工骚乱的报告。
由 J. MacGregor 撰写。由 M. Gibson 转呈
致
先生，
关于本区的劳工骚乱，谨就1925年2月26日的备忘录，呈报如下信息：
(1). 并无信息显示罢工者属于任何特定工会，或曾在区内任何地点聚集。收到关于1925年2月14日丰田棉纺厂（Toyoda Cotton Mill）罢工的情报称，在工人出厂前，有一名女学生在该厂内活动。该学生是谁或来自哪所学校，无法查明。
(2). 纠纷的起因可归咎于戈登路（Gordon Road）区日本纱厂工人的煽动。
(3). 关于上海皮革公司（Shanghai Leather Co.）的罢工，不满情绪和恐吓是其原因。丰田厂的工人中并无明显的不满情绪，且由于宣布全面停工，恐吓行为很少。
(4). 区内没有示威游行或任何宣传迹象。

to resume work, were it not for the Chapel Police who took charge of

pages.en:
Sir,

A strike of workpeople employed at the Toyoda
Cotton Spinning and Weaving Company's mill, 200 Jessfield
Road, commenced on the night of February 15, 1925.
Following the stoppage of work serious disturbances
occurred which resulted in injuries being sustained by
nine Japanese connected with the mill, one of whom was
shot, and two seriously assaulted about the head and
body and thrown into the Soochow Creek. One of the last
mentioned, named Yoshoji Harada, succumbed to his injuries
on March 1, 1925. During and for some days previous to
the strike, Chinese Police had been continuously on duty
on the Toyoda Cotton Mill premises which are situated
outside the boundary of the International Settlement and
when the strikers and their supporters behaving riotous
about eight armed men from the Chinese Police Station
were on duty at the entrance to the mill. Police from
the International Settlement went to the scene of disorder
and arrested nine persons, eight of whom were mill workers
who were caught in the act of destroying machinery or in
other ways creating breaches of the peace. These nine
persons were subsequently charged at the Mixed Court with
"Riotous Behaviour" contrary to Article 164 and "Doing
Malicious Damage to Property" contrary to Article 405 of
the Chinese Provisional Criminal Code and were sentenced
eight to three months imprisonment or a fine of $100.00
pages.zh:
先生，

受雇于极司菲尔路200号丰田棉纺织株式会社（Toyoda Cotton Spinning and Weaving Company）工厂的工人罢工，始于1925年2月15日晚。
停工后发生了严重的骚乱，导致与该厂有关的九名日本人受伤，其中一人被枪击，两人头部和身体遭受严重殴打并被扔进苏州河。最后提到的这名伤者名为原田芳次（Yoshoji Harada，音译），于1925年3月1日伤重不治。在罢工期间及此前数日，中国警察一直在位于国际租界边界之外的丰田棉纺厂 premises 连续执勤，当罢工者及其支持者行为暴乱时，约有八名武装人员从中国警察局派出在工厂入口处执勤。国际租界的警察前往骚乱现场，逮捕了九人，其中八人为工厂工人，他们是在破坏机器或以其他方式制造破坏和平行为时被当场抓获的。这九人随后在会审公廨被指控违反《中华民国暂行新刑律》第164条“聚众滋扰”和第405条“故意毁坏财物”，其中八人被判处三个月监禁或罚款100.00美元

pages.en:
each and one to six months imprisonment or a fine
of $200.00. The Chinese Police who had been regularly
on duty at the mill and who were in a position to
know what was going on and to anticipate any disturbance
did not arrest any of the persons concerned in the
rioting either during or after the strike. A man named
Sung Ah S(        ) employed as a mill hand at the
Toyoda Cotton Mill and residing in the Tsau Ka Jau
(        ) Village(O.O.L.) was arrested on a charge
of intimidation by the Chinese Police in the Brennan
Road Village (O.O.L.) on February 19 but whilst being
taken by a Sergeant and Constable to the Poh Sing Ching
(        ) Police Station he escaped from custody and has
not been recaptured. A man named Sung Liang Wei(        ),
Assistant Director of the Woo Si Koong Yeu(        ) Day
and Night School, Penang Road, and was also connected with
the Labourers Club, Tan Tsz Wan(        ), Chapel, and
who was chief spokesman at strikers' meetings held in
Chapei, was arrested on February 19 in Chapei. Enquiries
made during the strike went to show that he was one of
the most prominent strike leaders and applications were
made to the Chapei Police and the Ching Tsa Ting by the
Shanghai Municipal Police to hand over Sung Liang Wei for
trial in the Mixed Court of the International Settlement
on February 19, February 20, February 23, February 27,
March 12, March 17 and March 20. These applications were
all refused and on the last occasion the S.M.P. represen-
tatives were informed that Sung Liang Wei had been released
by order of the Chief of Police at the request of the
Chinese General Chamber of Commerce and Japanese mill owners.
The Chinese General Chamber of Commerce and a leading
pages.zh: 每人，一人被判处六个月监禁或罚款200.00美元。那些定期在工厂执勤、有能力了解事态发展并预见任何骚乱的中国警察，在罢工期间或之后并未逮捕任何参与骚乱的人员。一名名为沈阿四（Sung Ah S，音译，括号内原文不清）的男子，受雇于丰田棉纺厂做杂工，居住在周家桥村（Tsau Ka Jau，音译，括号内原文不清）（越界筑路区 O.O.L.），于2月19日在布伦南路村（Brennan Road Village，音译，括号内原文不清）（越界筑路区 O.O.L.）被中国警察以恐吓罪逮捕，但在由一名巡长和巡警押送往北新泾（Poh Sing Ching，音译，括号内原文不清）警察局途中逃脱监管，至今未被重新抓获。一名名为孙良惠（Sung Liang Wei，音译，括号内原文不清）的男子，是槟榔路（Penang Road）福西工友夜校（Woo Si Koong Yeu，音译，括号内原文不清）的副主任，也与谭子彦（Tan Tsz Wan，音译，括号内原文不清）教堂的工人俱乐部有关联，他是闸北举行的罢工者集会的主要发言人，于2月19日在闸北被捕。罢工期间进行的调查显示，他是最突出的罢工领导人之一，上海公共租界工部局警务处于2月19日、2月20日、2月23日、2月27日、3月12日、3月17日和3月20日向闸北警察厅和警察厅提出申请，要求移交孙良惠以便在国际租界会审公廨受审。这些申请均被拒绝，在最后一次，工部局警务处代表获悉，应中国总商会和日本纱厂厂主的要求，警察总监已下令释放孙良惠。中国总商会和一家主要的

pages.en:
official of the Naga Tata Kaisha Co. later denied that
any such request had been made. Since his release,
Sung Liang Tei has been known to frequent the Labourers'
Club, San Tuh Lee(          ), Tan Tsz Man(          ),
Chapel, and he was selected amongst others to represent
local Japanese cotton mill workers at the May Day
Celebration in Canton and left Shanghai for that port
on April 24.
    There are a number of warrants in the hands
of the Police for the arrest of persons concerned in
the strike of cotton mill workers which occurred in
February of this year, but the culprits apparently
feel safer and more immune from arrest in Chinese
territory and therefore do not venture into the
Settlement.
    I beg to point out that the procedure hitherto
observed is that correspondence of this nature has
been conducted through the Senior Consul.

                Yours faithfully,
pages.zh:
长崎纺织株式会社（Naga Tata Kaisha Co.，音译）官员后来否认曾提出此类请求。自获释以来，据悉孙良惠（Sung Liang Tei，原文拼写变化）经常出入三德里（San Tuh Lee，音译，括号内原文不清）、谭子彦（Tan Tsz Man，音译，括号内原文不清）教堂的工人俱乐部，他被选中作为当地日本棉纺厂工人的代表之一，前往广州参加五一庆祝活动，并于4月24日离开上海前往该港口。
警方手中握有多张逮捕令，用于逮捕参与今年二月发生的棉纺厂工人罢工的人员，但罪犯们显然觉得在中国领土上更安全、更不易被捕，因此不敢进入租界。
谨指出，迄今为止遵循的程序是，此类信函往来均通过总领事进行。

此致，
敬礼，

Letter from the Kiangsu Commissioner of Foreign Affairs

Sir,
A strike of work people employed at the Toyoda
Cotton Spinning and Weaving Company's Mill, 200 Jessfield Road,
occurred on the night of February 10, 1925. Serious disturbances
followed the stoppage of work and resulted in injuries to nine
Japanese connected with the mill one of whom was shot, one
seriously assaulted about the head and body, and one beaten
about the head and thrown into the Soochow Creek. The last
mentioned whose name was S. Takeya, succumbed to his injuries on
the afternoon of March 1, 1925. Nine persons were arrested
by the Shanghai Municipal Police at the time the disturbances
were going on and were charged with "Riotous Behaviour" contrary
to Article 164 of the Chinese Provisional Criminal Code and
further charged with "Doing Malicious Damage to Property"
contrary to Article 405 of the Chinese Provisional Criminal Code.
The trial of the nine men took place on March 25, when eight
of the accused were fined $100.00 or three months imprisonment
each and one was fined $200.00 or six months imprisonment.
A man named Sung Ah S(沈阿四) employed as a mill hand at
the Toyoda Cotton Mill and residing in the Tsau Ka Jau(周家橋)
Village (O.O.L.) was arrested by the Chinese Police on a charge
of intimidation in the Brennan Road Village (O.O.L.) Whilst
being taken to Poh Sing Ching(北新涇) Police Station by a
sergeant and Constable of the Chinese Police, Sung Ah S escaped
from custody and has not been recaptured.
Enquiries made by the Police during the strike go to
show that prominent amongst the ringleaders was a man named

5月13日 5
江苏省外交专员关于逮捕罢工领导人的来信。
督察长 Sullivan
先生，
受雇于极司菲尔路200号丰田棉纺织株式会社工厂的工人罢工，发生于1925年2月10日晚。停工后发生了严重的骚乱，导致与该厂有关的九名日本人受伤，其中一人被枪击，一人头部和身体遭受严重殴打，一人头部被打并被扔进苏州河。最后提到的这名伤者名为 S. Takeya（竹谷，音译），于1925年3月1日下午伤重不治。九人在骚乱进行时被上海公共租界工部局警务处逮捕，并被指控违反《中华民国暂行新刑律》第164条“聚众滋扰”，并进一步被指控违反该刑律第405条“故意毁坏财物”。对这九人的审判于3月25日进行，其中八名被告各被罚款100.00美元或判处三个月监禁，一人被罚款200.00美元或判处六个月监禁。一名名为沈阿四（Sung Ah S）的男子，受雇于丰田棉纺厂做杂工，居住在周家桥（Tsau Ka Jau）村（越界筑路区 O.O.L.），在布伦南路村（Brennan Road Village）（越界筑路区 O.O.L.）被中国警察以恐吓罪逮捕。在由中国警察的一名巡长和巡警押送往北新泾（Poh Sing Ching）警察局途中，沈阿四逃脱监管，至今未被重新抓获。
警方在罢工期间进行的调查显示，在头目中突出的是名为

pages.en:
-2-

Sung Liang Wei(孫良惠), who was Assistant Director of the Foo
Si Koong Yeu(福西工友) Day and Night School, Penang Road,
and was also connected with the Labourers' Club, Tan Tsz Yan
(譚子彥), Chapel. He was the Chief spokesman at strikers'
meetings held in Chapel. On February 19, 1925 Sung Liang Wei
was arrested in Chapel by the Shanghai Municipal Police assisted
by the Chapei Police and charged with intimidating the workers
employed at the Naga Wata Kaisha Company's Cotton Mills .
On the afternoon of the same day a request was made by the
S.M.P. at the 4th Division Police Headquarters for Sung to be
handed over for trial in the Mixed Court of the International
Settlement. The representatives of the S.M.P. were referred to
the Ching Tsa Ting(警察廳 Chinese City Police). On February 20
1925 an application was made at the Ching Tsa Ting(警察廳)
by the S.M.P. who were in possession of a despatch letter issued
by the Mixed Court for the handing over of Sung Liang Wei.
The application was refused on the grounds that Sung had not been
examined and the Chinese Police stated that they wished to
inspect books and papers found in Sung's possession at the time
of his arrest. A further application was made on February 23,
1925 when Shun Shing Ting(孫慶鼎), an assistant magistrate,
stated that he had received instructions from the Chief of Police
that the man must not be handed over yet as it was a very serious
case and searching inquiries were necessary and that in all
probability a charge would be laid against Sung in the Chinese
City. Another application was made by representatives of the
pages.zh:
-2-

孙良惠（Sung Liang Wei）的男子，他是槟榔路福西工友（Foo Si Koong Yeu）日夜学校的副主任，也与谭子彦（Tan Tsz Yan）教堂的工人俱乐部有关联。他是教堂举行的罢工者集会的主要发言人。1925年2月19日，孙良惠在教堂被上海公共租界工部局警务处在闸北警察协助下逮捕，并被指控恐吓长崎纺织株式会社（Naga Wata Kaisha Company，音译）棉纺厂的工人。
同日下午，工部局警务处在第四分区警察总局提出要求，希望将孙移交至国际租界会审公廨受审。工部局警务处的代表被引荐至警察厅（Chinese City Police）。1925年2月20日，工部局警务处持会审公廨发出的移交函，向警察厅申请移交孙良惠。该申请以孙尚未受审为由被拒绝，中国警察表示希望检查孙被捕时随身携带的书籍和文件。1925年2月23日再次提出申请，当时助理审判员孙庆鼎（Shun Shing Ting，音译）表示，他已接到警察总监的指示，此人暂时不得移交，因为这是一起非常严重的案件，需要进行深入调查，并且很可能将在华界对孙提出指控。代表们又提出了一次申请，由

pages.en:
-3-

S.M.P. to the Ching Tsa Ting on February 27. The application
was again refused, Magistrate Tuan stating that a letter had been
sent to the Nanking Authorities and a reply containing instructions
was awaited. Further unsuccessful applications for Sung Liang
Wei (孫良惠) to be handed over for trial at the International
Mixed Court were made on March 12 and March 17, 1925. On March 20,
1925, the S.M.P. were informed that Sung Liang Wei had been
released by order of the Chief of Police at the request of the Chin-
ese General Chamber of Commerce and Japanese Mill Owners. The
Chinese General Chamber of Commerce and a leading official of
the Naga Wata Kaisha Co. later denied that any such request
had been made. Since his release Sung Liang Wei has been known
to frequent the Labourers' Club, San Tuh Lee (三德里), Tan Tsz Wan
(譚子灣), Chapel, and he was selected amongst others to
represent local Japanese cotton mill workers at the May Day
Celebration in Canton and left for that port on April 24.
There are a number of warrants in the hands of the
Police for the arrest of persons concerned in the recent cotton
mill workers' strike, but as far as can be ascertained the
wanted men are not in the International Settlement.

I am, Sir,
Your obedient servant,

D. I.

D. C. I.

-3-

2月27日，上海公共租界工部局警务处致静安寺捕房。申请再次被拒，段法官称已致函南京当局，正等待包含指示的回复。1925年3月12日和3月17日，又多次申请将孙良惠移交国际混合法庭受审，均未成功。1925年3月20日，上海公共租界工部局警务处获悉，应中国总商会和日本纱厂主的要求，警察总监下令释放了孙良惠。中国总商会和长棉株式会社（Naga Wata Kaisha Co.）的一名高级官员后来否认曾提出此类请求。自获释以来，已知孙良惠经常出入三德里、谭子湾教堂的劳工俱乐部，他与其他几人一起被选为代表当地日本棉纺厂工人参加广州五一庆祝活动的代表，并于4月24日启程前往该港口。

警方手中握有多张逮捕令，用于逮捕涉及近期棉纺厂工人罢工的人员，但据查，通缉犯并不在国际租界内。

先生，
您顺从的仆人，

March 7, 1935. 198

REPORT ON Rumours of unrest in the labour situation Toyoda Mill
200 Jessfield Road.

Made by D. MacGregor. Forwarded by [Signature]
Inspector.

Sir,

With reference to information received from C.D.I. Burnside
regarding rumours of unrest amongst the Chinese employees of the
Toyoda Cotton Mill 200 Jessfield Road I beg to state that this
rumour has been verified.

From the information received that the employees maintain that
they are not being treated as they were before the strike.
There complaints are:-

(1). There are only two badges issued to 60 for the use of
the lavatory, without this badge they cannot use same.

(2). A 1 cent increase promised them has not been paid.

(3). They want an hour for meals instead of the present half
hour.

(4). They are dissatisfied with the fact that they are not
allowed admission into the works without showing both badge and
book. Previously either badge or book was sufficient.

Most of the dissatisfaction appears to be in the Carding
Room, where the strike commenced before. My informant states that
the strike is to take place on Monday afternoon. Special precau-
-tions are being taken. A C.D.C. is detailed for that vicinity.

I am Sir,
Yours obediently,
[Signature]
D.C.

D.C.I.

关于杰斯菲尔德路200号丰田纱厂劳工局势动荡谣言的报告。

由 D. MacGregor 撰写。由 [签名] 督察转呈。

先生，

鉴于从刑事侦缉处 Burnside 处收到的关于杰斯菲尔德路200号丰田棉纺厂中国雇员中流传动荡谣言的情报，谨此声明该谣言已得到证实。

根据收到的情报，雇员们声称他们受到的待遇不如罢工前。他们的投诉如下：

(1). 60人仅发放两个如厕徽章，无此徽章者不得使用厕所。

(2). 承诺给他们增加的1分钱工资并未支付。

(3). 他们希望用餐时间为一小时，而非目前的半小时。

(4). 他们对必须同时出示徽章和工牌才能进入工厂的规定感到不满。此前只需出示其中一项即可。

大多数不满情绪似乎集中在梳棉间，此前的罢工即由此开始。我的线人称罢工将于周一下午举行。正在采取特别预防措施。已指派一名刑事侦缉警员负责该区域。

先生，
您顺从的，
[签名]
D.C.

D.C.I.

using the lavatory, no further special attention would
be given this point. Chief Inspector has sent a man

REPORT ON Strikes at Toyolo Cotton Mill 300 Jessfield Road.

Made by D.J. MacGregor.          Forwarded by L.J. Chinnell

Sir,

    At 2 P.M. February 15, 1925 a telephone message was receiv-
-ed from the Toyolo Cotton Mill 300 Jessfield Road, reporting
that rumours were current that agitators were advocating a
general strike.

    Enquiries were made immediately, but as far as could be
ascertained the rumour was unfounded. As a precautionary measure
a C.D.C. was detailed to stop in the Mill.

    At 7.50 P.M. a telephone message was received from I.S.C.
S/S Liang Ping stating that he had arrested a Chinese for
sabotage and that there was a feeling of restlessness amongst
the night shift workers.

    Accompanied by S.P.C.'s Layne and Archer and three Sikhs
Constables, I proceeded to the Mill and found a party of about
700 congregated outside the main entrance. Giving the Constables
instructions to guard the most important sites in the Mill, I
got in the center of the strikers and to a certain extent
appeased them and quite a few of them left quickly. In the mean-
-time trouble had arisen in the Carding room. The employees
there commenced to break up the machinery.

    At this point I may mention that enquiries show that the
Carding room was the center of the agitation, spreading rapidly
to other departments. As the sabotage started a rush was made
for the gates by the women resulting in the Chinese Police firing
one shot in the air. This action appeared to have enraged the
strikers. I made a further attempt and very nearly succeeded in

由 D.J. MacGregor 撰写。          由 L.J. Chinnell 转呈

先生：

    1925年2月15日下午2时，接到极司非尔路300号丰田纱厂（Toyolo Cotton Mill）的电话消息，称有谣言流传，煽动者正在鼓动总罢工。

    随即进行了调查，但据查该谣言并无根据。作为预防措施，指派了一名华籍侦探（C.D.C.）驻守在该厂内。

    晚上7时50分，接到印度巡捕（I.S.C.）三等巡长梁平（Liang Ping）的电话，称他已逮捕一名从事破坏活动的华人，且夜班工人中情绪不安。

    在巡官莱恩（Layne）和阿彻（Archer）以及三名锡克教巡捕的陪同下，我前往该厂，发现约有700人聚集在大门外。我指令巡捕守卫厂内最重要的地点，随后进入罢工人群中心，在一定程度上安抚了他们，相当一部分人迅速离去。与此同时，梳棉车间发生了骚乱。那里的员工开始破坏机器。

    在此须提及，调查显示梳棉车间是煽动活动的中心，并迅速蔓延至其他部门。由于破坏活动开始，女工们冲向大门，导致中国警察向空中鸣枪一响。这一举动似乎激怒了罢工者。我再次尝试，并几乎成功让

sending the away quietly when the Chapai Police opened fire, again
discharging 4 rounds in the air. By this time most of the workers
had left the Mill. Congregating outside the Mill, the strikers
commenced to break windows, and throw stones. The Bubbling Well
Station car which was left on Jessfield Road was pushed into
the Soochow Creek but was later salvaged, very little damage
being done.

During the time the mob was at the highest pitch of ex-
-citement, seven Japanese drove up in a car to the Mill gates.
The car was held up by the mob. The Mill Doctor named T. Horie
was seriously assaulted about the head and body. An Assistant
Manager named S. Syoshi was shot through the right side, the
bullet penetrating the lung and lodging in the vicinity of the
spine. From the wound the weapon used was undoubtedly a .38
revolver or automatic. This case is considered critical. Another
Japanese named Hayeya was beaten about the head and thrown
into the Soochow Creek, being later rescued by a boatman.

In all 9 Japanese were injured. Those mentioned above
being the most serious.

From enquiries made it appears that at 7.30 P.M. February
15, 1925 a number of agitators got into the Carding room by clim-
-bing over the Mill wall. A woman of the student type is said
to have been amongst the agitators waving a white flag. The
cause of the strike can undoubtedly be connected with the labour
movement which prevails in Shanghai at present.

他们安静离开时，闸北警察开火，再次向空中发射了4发子弹。此时，大多数工人已离开工厂。罢工者聚集在厂外，开始砸碎窗户并投掷石块。留在极司非尔路上的静安寺巡捕房汽车被推入苏州河，但后来被打捞上岸，受损甚微。

在暴民情绪最高涨的时候，七名日本人驾车来到工厂大门。汽车被暴民拦住。名为 T. Horie 的厂医头部和身体遭受严重殴打。名为 S. Syoshi 的副经理右侧中弹，子弹穿透肺部并卡在脊柱附近。从伤口判断，所用武器无疑是一把.38口径左轮手枪或自动手枪。此案情况危急。另一名名为 Hayeya 的日本人头部遭殴打并被扔进苏州河，后被一名船夫救起。

共有9名日本人受伤。上述人员伤势最为严重。

经查询，似乎是在1925年2月15日晚上7时30分，数名煽动者翻越工厂围墙进入梳棉车间。据说煽动者中有一名女学生模样的人挥舞着白旗。罢工的原因无疑与目前上海盛行的劳工运动有关。

The management of the Mill in an interview stated that
they could not understand why the employees came out as they
had been paid the best wages in Shanghai.

At 8.30 P.M. re-enforcement arrived from the Station
and in a few minutes the vicinity was cleared of the strikers.
In all there are about 2000, male and female employed in the
Mill.

The day shift finished at 6 P.M. February 15, 1925 and
did not know anything about the outbreak.

On returning to resumed work at 5.30 A.M. February 16,
1925 they were informed that a general lock out had been Autho-
-rised, but that they (the day shift) would be compensated. They
left very orderly. Nine men have been arrested and will be
brought up before the Mixed Court to day (February 16th) on
charges of sabotage and disorderly conduct. A remand will be
asked for, to bring them before the Japanese Assessor.
