法庭于下午5点45分复庭。

十五名男子，即戴宝成（Tai Pao Sung），34岁，苦力；夏宗荣（Nyi Tsong Yoong），23岁，翻译；许品高（Tsu Ping Kan），25岁，苦力；范凤义（Van Vong Yi），26岁，苦力；高雨田（Kao Yu Dien），35岁，苦力；张文金（Tsang Vung Kyung），27岁，苦力；宋荣之（Sung Yoong Si），27岁，苦力；乔云之（Kyau Yoong Ts），28岁，苦力；陈竹山（Tsung Tuh San），25岁，苦力；董泰达（Dong Tuh Dah），28岁，翻译；陶阿毛（Dau Ah Mau），22岁，苦力；杜万荣（Doo Van Yoong），27岁，苦力；江海煌（Chang Hai Hwang），20岁，苦力；陈荣田（Lau Yoong Dien），27岁，苦力；以及张三（Tsangl Ah San），28岁，苦力，被指控如下：
指控他们于1925年2月19日在引翔港（Ying Ziang Kong）集会，并在警方当局命令解散该集会后实施暴力行为，违反《中华民国暂行新刑律》第165条。

科维先生：由于这是一起重要案件，我请求延期审理，以便我更彻底地调查此案。
梅特兰先生：我想指出，这些人自2月19日起一直被拘留，我的朋友有充足的时间调查此案。
陪审推事：我们将继续审理。
梅特兰先生：这些人被指控犯有暴乱罪。

传召警佐道格拉斯（Douglas）作证，他说：2月19日下午3点，我在引翔港巡捕房，查茨伍（Tsah Ts Woo）在那里被捕。约有700人聚集在租界边界处的巡捕房外。人群的大部分位于租界内。下午3点，这群暴徒袭击了巡捕房，推倒竹篱笆，冲进巡捕房，直到中国警察发射数发子弹后，他们才被驱赶回篱笆处。我看到两个人在带领他们，他们是高雨田和陈竹山。当他们被驱赶回篱笆处时，他们留在那里并采取威胁姿态。最终，我派信使前往杨树浦巡捕房求援。下午3点50分，约翰逊（Johnson）巡官、警佐格鲁布（Grubb）和一队警察到达。约翰逊巡官命令人群解散，由一名中国侦探担任翻译。他们被告知，如果不解散，将向他们开枪。随后工部局警察冲向人群，中国警察开火，并向人群上方连续射击。这15名被告因最不愿解散而被捕。警察深入租界内部约400至500码，人群随即四散奔逃。这些人当时在附近被捕，并由中国警察移交给我们要。在约翰逊巡官到达之前，我

accompanied by Inspector Wei and two Chinese detectives. I saw
two Chinese detectives mixing with the crowd and from them I got
certain information.
Mr. Maitland: No other damage done besides that to the fence?
Witness: No other damage was done.
Counsel: You said Kao was a leader. Did you question him?
Witness: Yes. He said the strike was started by Kiu Ching
Chang ( ). He said he was at the club on February 9 when
Kiu informed him that probably they would be going on strike on
the following day. He visited the place at 603 Meichow Road on
the 1st and 2nd days of the strike. That was the only time. They
paid six cents per day to the school.
I also questioned Tsung Tuh San. He said he lost a leg in
a cotton mill four years ago. He was living as a hawker. He lived
at the Workers Union school. One hundred workers visited this
place daily and on the occasions of meetings the attendance was
regular. Since he joined the school three meetings had been held.
A man named Kiu Ching Chang acted as messenger to the school and
brought in a quantity of circulars relating to the strike. On
one occasion the papers came from the Labourers Association in
Kiaochow Road. On February 11 he went to San Teh Lee near the
Dah Kong mill to see some friend and on that occasion he had a
quantity of papers which had been given to him to distribute.
One of them was entitled, "The Freedom of the Proletariat."

Cross-examined by Mr. Covey: How many persons were on the road?
Witness: I would estimate the crowd at 700 to 800.
Counsel: And there was much going and coming?
Witness: They did not get a chance to come back again.
Counsel: And you made no arrests at the time?
Witness: They were all arrested at that time.
Counsel: I thought you said the Chinese authorities handed
them over to the Police?
Witness: Some were arrested with the assistance of the Chinese
authorities, taken to the Chinese Police Station and then handed
over to us.
Counsel: I think they were all from one mill?
Witness: One or two were from the Dah Kong mill, but most of
them were from the Yue Foong mill. One of them is not connected
with any mill at all.
Counsel: Did you question them with regard to this rioting?
Witness: Yes, I questioned them all.
Counsel: Did you question them with regard to the reasons of

Witness: Yes.
Counsel: Did they mention anything about ill-treatment?
Witness: No mention of ill-treatment was made to me at all.
Counsel: Anything of the many hours they work?
Witness: No mention of the hours they work was made to me.

由魏（Wei）巡官和两名中国侦探陪同。我看到两名中国侦探混入人群中，并从他们那里获得了一些情报。
梅特兰先生：除了篱笆受损外，没有其他损坏吗？
证人：没有其他损坏。
辩护律师：你说高是领导者。你审问了他吗？
证人：是的。他说罢工是由邱景章（Kiu Ching Chang）（原文不清）发起的。他说2月9日他在俱乐部时，邱通知他他们可能在第二天罢工。他在罢工的第一和第二天去过梅州路603号。那是唯一的一次。他们每天向学校支付六分钱。
我也审问了陈竹山。他说四年前他在一家棉纺厂失去了一条腿。他以小贩为生。他住在工会学校。每天有一百名工人访问这个地方，开会时出席人数通常很多。自从他加入学校以来，已经举行了三次会议。一个叫邱景章的人充当学校的信使，带来了大量关于罢工的传单。有一次，这些文件来自胶州路的劳工协会。2月11日，他去大康纱厂附近的三德里（San Teh Lee）看望朋友，当时他手头有一批发给他的待分发文件。其中一份标题为《无产阶级的自由》。

由科维先生交叉询问：路上有多少人？
证人：我估计人群有700到800人。
辩护律师：并且有很多人来回走动？
证人：他们没有机会再回来。
辩护律师：当时你没有进行逮捕吗？
证人：他们当时全都被捕了。
辩护律师：我以为你说是中国当局将他们移交给警察的？
证人：有些人是在中国当局的协助下被捕的，被带到中国巡捕房，然后移交给我们要。
辩护律师：我想他们都来自同一家工厂？
证人：有一两个人来自大康纱厂，但大多数人来自裕丰纱厂（Yue Foong mill）。其中一人与任何工厂都没有关系。
辩护律师：你就这次暴乱审问了他们吗？
证人：是的，我审问了所有人。
辩护律师：你就罢工的原因审问了他们吗？
证人：是的。
辩护律师：他们提到任何关于虐待的事情吗？
证人：完全没有向我提及虐待之事。
辩护律师：关于他们工作很长时间的事呢？
证人：没有向我提及他们的工作时长。
辩护律师：关于他们日复一日工作，去领薪水却领不到的事？

their pay not getting it?
Witness: No.
Inspector Johnson, of Yangtsepoo Police Station, called,
said: I was called by chit at the time of the rioting. When I
arrived there was a crowd of about 700 to 800 shouting and jeering,
I broke my way through and got to the front. I was accompanied
by an armed party of Sikhs and foreigners. I stood in front of
the crowd a few minutes and listened to them. I then called C.D.C.
Ming Tuh to tell them that if they did not disperse we would fire
upon the crowd. Two men shouted out, "Don't move." I called out
to one of the men not to move, and at the same time I sang out
to the Chinese Police to fire. They opened fire over the heads
of the crowd. We made a baton charge and arrested them.
C.D.C. Zung Ming Tuh said; I mingled with the crowd. The
trouble was due to Tsah Ts Woo having been arrested by the Chinese
Police as he was holding a meeting on a piece of vacant ground.
Kao Yu Dien and another told the crowd not to move and to kill
the detectives, to shoot them.
Cross-examined by Mr. Covey, witness said: I was amongst the
crowd for half an hour. The trouble was due to Tsah Ts Woo's
arrest. He is a teacher and head of the Union. He is the chief
of all.
Counsel: In that case he will be entirely to blame for the
trouble?
Witness: The trouble was caused through people holding a
meeting.
Counsel: The meeting an ordinary meeting?
Witness: This was not like another meeting. This was a meeting
of labourers.
Counsel: Did he call the meeting?
Witness: Yes, he is the leader.
Counsel: Did you see the accused?
Witness: Yes.
Counsel: You said something about shooting. They could not
very well shoot without any guns?
Witness: I could not know that they had no arms. After the
fence was pulled down they had sticks.
C.D.C. Kung Tuh Piau (耿德標) said: I mixed with the crowd.
They were talking about the release of the man Tsah Ts Woo, and
said that if Tsah was not released, when the foreigners came out
they would kill the foreigners. These words were said by Kao
Yu Dien and Tsung Tuh San. These two men told the others not to
disperse. The crowd then broke down the fence. Later Chinese
and foreign Police arrested the 15 men.
Addressing the Court, Mr. Maitland here said that he had
other witnesses here but it would be a waste of time to call
them all unless the Court would like to hear them.
The Assessor: No, you need not call them.
This was the case for the prosecution.
The accused were then examined by turns by the Magistrate.

证人：没有。
传召杨树浦巡捕房的约翰逊巡官作证，他说：暴乱发生时，我接到便条通知。当我到达时，约有700到800人在呼喊和嘲弄，我挤过人群来到前面。我由一队武装锡克教徒和外国人陪同。我在人群前站了几分钟，听他们说话。然后我叫来中国侦探明笃（Ming Tuh，音译）告诉他们，如果不解散，我们将向人群开枪。两个人喊道：“不要动。”我叫其中一个人不要动，同时大声命令中国警察开枪。他们向人群头顶上方开火。我们持警棍冲锋并逮捕了他们。
中国侦探长钟明笃（Zung Ming Tuh，音译）说：我混入人群中。麻烦起因于查茨伍在一块空地上举行会议时被中国警察逮捕。高雨田和另一个人告诉人群不要动，并杀死侦探，枪杀他们。
由科维先生交叉询问，证人说：我在人群中呆了半小时。麻烦是由查茨伍被捕引起的。他是一名教师兼工会负责人。他是所有人的头目。
辩护律师：那样的话，他将完全对麻烦负责？
证人：麻烦是由人们举行会议引起的。
辩护律师：会议是普通会议吗？
证人：这不像其他会议。这是工人的会议。
辩护律师：是他召集的会议吗？
证人：是的，他是领导者。
辩护律师：你看到被告了吗？
证人：是的。
辩护律师：你提到了射击。他们没有枪很难射击吧？
证人：我无法知道他们没有武器。篱笆被推倒后，他们手里有棍棒。
中国侦探耿德標（Kung Tuh Piau）说：我混入人群中。他们在谈论释放查茨伍这个人，并说如果查不被释放，当外国人出来时，他们将杀死外国人。这些话是高雨田和陈竹山说的。这两人告诉其他人不要解散。随后人群推倒了篱笆。后来中国和外国警察逮捕了这15人。
梅特兰先生在此向法庭陈述，他还有其他证人在场，但如果法庭不想听取他们的证词，传唤所有人将是浪费时间。
陪审推事：不，你不必传唤他们。
至此，控方举证结束。
随后，裁判官依次讯问被告。

Tai Pau Sung denied causing the riot because of Tsah Ts
Woo's arrest. He was in the temple at the time. He did not see
any of the Police. He did not break down the bamboo fence.
Nyi Tsong Yoong: I did not see the Police. I was eating
food in the temple. I was stepping out of the temple when the
Police arrested me. I did not hear any detectives telling the
people to disperse. I went to the temple to make inquiries.
There were about 300 to 400 persons in the temple. The Chinese
Police came to the temple and arrested us. I do not know
anything of a labour meeting.
Tau Ping Kau said: When the Police began to fire I ran
away and was arrested. I happened to be passing the place. I do
not know anything about a labour meeting. I was there late.
Van Vong Yi said: I was called by Tai Pau Sung to go to
work. I did not hear the foreign or Chinese Police asking the
people to disperse. When the firing began I tried to run away
and was arrested.
Kao Yu Dien said: I requested the people not to riot. I did
not tell them to kill the detectives.
The Magistrate: Was it because Tsah Ts Woo was arrested
that you started this disturbance?
Accused: No. I told the people not to move and to keep quiet.
The Magistrate: According to your statement, then you must
be a law-abiding man: then why have you been arrested?
Accused made no reply.
Tsang Vung Kyung said: I did not hear the Police asking the
people to disperse.
Sung Yoong Si said: When I arrived I saw a disturbance and
I tried to pacify the people. We were fired upon and I was then
arrested. I had no time to run away. I do not know Tsah Ts Woo.
I did not see the fence broken down. I work in the machine
department of the Yue Fong mill. I am a peaceful man. I have
a nickname "Dah Woo Zong." (Big Monk.)
The Magistrate: You were one of the instigators of the riot?
Accused: No.
Kyau Yoong Ts said: I was not there at the time. I went
there afterwards. On February 19 I received a letter from some
one representing 40,000 labourers asking us interpreters not
to betray the workers. I felt sorry and did not know what to do.
I heard the Police asking us to disperse, but as I was in the
temple and as I am law-abiding, I did not run away.
Tsung Tuh San said: I was not at the meeting but at home,
about a mile from the meeting place. Tsah Ts Woo is one of our
masters. I was told that our teacher Tsah had been arrested. As
he is our teacher we tried to save him. I then went over to the
place but the fence was already pulled down.
The Magistrate: And was it your idea to cause a riot in
order to bring about the release of Tsah Ts Woo?
Accused: I went to see Tsah and saw a big crowd. Fearing

戴宝松（Tai Pau Sung）否认因查茨武（Tsah Ts Woo，音译）被捕而引发骚乱。事发时他在庙里。他没有看到任何巡捕。他没有拆毁竹篱笆。
倪宗荣（Nyi Tsong Yoong，音译）：我没有看到巡捕。我当时在庙里吃饭。当我走出庙门时，巡捕逮捕了我。我没有听到任何侦探命令人群解散。我去庙里是为了打听消息。庙里大约有300到400人。中国巡捕来到庙里逮捕了我们。我对劳工集会一事一无所知。
陶平久（Tau Ping Kau，音译）说：当巡捕开始开枪时，我逃跑了并被逮捕。我碰巧路过那里。我对劳工集会一无所知。我到那里时已经很晚了。
范万义（Van Vong Yi，音译）说：是戴宝松叫我去干活的。我没有听到外国或中国巡捕要求人群解散。当枪声响起时，我试图逃跑并被逮捕。
高玉典（Kao Yu Dien，音译）说：我请求人们不要暴动。我没有让他们去杀侦探。
法官：是因为查茨武被捕，你们才挑起这场骚乱的吗？
被告：不。我告诉人们不要走动，保持安静。
法官：根据你的陈述，那你应该是一个守法的人：那你为什么会被捕？
被告没有回答。
曾云庆（Tsang Vung Kyung，音译）说：我没有听到巡捕要求人群解散。
宋永思（Sung Yoong Si，音译）说：当我到达时，我看到发生了骚乱，我试图安抚民众。我们遭到了射击，随后我被捕。我没有时间逃跑。我不认识查茨武。我没有看到篱笆被拆毁。我在岳丰纱厂机器部工作。我是一个安分守己的人。我有一个绰号叫“大和尚”（Dah Woo Zong）。
法官：你是这次骚乱的煽动者之一吗？
被告：不。
乔永慈（Kyau Yoong Ts，音译）说：当时我不在那里。我是后来去的。2月19日，我收到一封代表四万名工人的来信，要求我们这些翻译不要出卖工人。我感到难过，不知如何是好。我听到巡捕要求我们解散，但因为我在庙里，而且我是个守法的人，所以我没有逃跑。
宗德山（Tsung Tuh San，音译）说：我没有参加会议，而是在家里，距离会场大约一英里。查茨武是我们的师傅之一。有人告诉我，我们的师傅查先生被捕了。因为他是我们的师傅，我们试图救他。于是我去了现场，但篱笆已经被拆倒了。
法官：那么，为了促使查茨武获释而制造骚乱，是你的主意吗？
被告：我去看望查先生，看到一大群人。由于害怕

a riot, I tried to prevent rioting.
    The Magistrate: And did you say that unless Tsah was
released, you would kill the detectives?
    Accused: No.
    The Magistrate: Did you tell the workers to start rioting
and to pull down the fence?
    Accused: I went there late. The fence was already pulled
down. There has been some misunderstanding over what I said.
When the workers wanted to make a rush, I told them not to move
and not to rush inside. They still wanted to rush in.
    Dong Tuh Dah said: I was the first man to enter the
Station. On the 19th a man came to me with a letter signed
"Labourer." It was addressed to coolies as well as to labourers.
It stated that as we were all Chinese we must sympathise and help
the labourers, and that if I did not do so, my life would be in
danger. I then called upon the manager of the mill and he told
me not to pay any attention to the letter and asked me to attend
the meeting to find out what the workers would do and to make a
report to him. At 11.30 a.m. I was standing on a grave mound.
There was a big crowd. The Chinese Police questioned me and asked
me whether I was intimidating the workers. I said that I had been
sent by the manager and told them everything. The Police then said
I had better go and explain at the Police Station. I then went with
him. I was in a room at the Station and saw many of the workers
break down the fence and the Police opened fire. I was in the
Station all the time. I tried to stop the people but could not do
anything. After the trouble a number of persons were arrested.
I was at the Station all the time. The detectives can be questioned
about this. My statement is the truth.
    Called by the Magistrate, C.D.C. Zung Ming Tuh said: The
accused was arrested at the same time as Tsah Ts Woo on the 19th.
The accused: I was not there. I do not know Tsah Ts Woo.
    The Magistrate: So that you were arrested and did not go
to the Police Station voluntarily? And you were holding meetings
with Tsah.
    Accused made no reply.
    Dau Ah Mau said: I was at Ying Ziang Kong buying socks.
I heard a noise and went outside the shop to see what it was and
I was arrested. I saw foreign and Chinese Police arresting people.
    Doo Van Yoong said: I was not present during the rioting
but went there after the firing. I went to the temple where I
was arrested. I did not hear the Police ask the people to
disperse. I was not at the meeting.
    Chang Hai Hwang said: I know nothing about the rioting.
I went out to buy some food at 4.30 p.m. I saw a crowd. I went
out to see what was the matter and I was arrested. I know nothing
about the fence.
    Lau Yoong Dien said: I was not present during the rioting.
I was in the temple. buying sugar cane and was arrested. I was
not present at the meeting. I know nothing about the fence.

发生暴动，我试图阻止暴乱。
    法官：你是否说过，除非释放查先生，否则你们就要杀死侦探？
    被告：不。
    法官：你是否告诉工人们开始暴动并拆毁篱笆？
    被告：我去得很晚。篱笆已经被拆倒了。对我所说的话存在一些误解。当工人们想要冲进去时，我告诉他们不要动，不要往里冲。但他们仍然想冲进去。
    董德达（Dong Tuh Dah，音译）说：我是第一个进入巡捕房的人。19日，一个人拿着一封署名为“劳工”的信来找我。这封信既是写给苦力的，也是写给工人的。信中说，既然我们都是中国人，我们必须同情并帮助工人，如果我不这样做，我的生命就会有危险。于是我去找了工厂经理，他告诉我不要理会那封信，并让我去参加集会，看看工人们会做什么，然后向他汇报。上午11点30分，我站在一个坟堆上。那里有一大群人。中国巡捕审问了我，问我是否在恐吓工人。我说我是经理派来的，并把一切都告诉了他们。巡捕随后说我最好去巡捕房解释一下。于是我就跟他去了。我在巡捕房的一个房间里，看到许多工人拆毁了篱笆，巡捕开了枪。我一直待在巡捕房里。我试图阻止众人，但无能为力。骚乱过后，许多人被捕。我一直待在巡捕房里。侦探们可以就此接受质询。我的陈述是真实的。
    应法官传唤，刑事侦缉处长钟明德（C.D.C. Zung Ming Tuh，音译）说：被告于19日与查茨武同时被捕。
    被告：我不在那里。我不认识查茨武。
    法官：所以你是被捕的，而不是自愿去巡捕房的？而且你曾与查先生举行会议。
    被告没有回答。
    杜阿毛（Dau Ah Mau，音译）说：我在英祥公（Ying Ziang Kong，音译）买袜子。我听到一阵喧闹声，便到店外查看是怎么回事，结果被捕了。我看到外国和中国巡捕正在逮捕人。
    杜万荣（Doo Van Yoong，音译）说：骚乱期间我不在场，而是在枪响之后去的。我去了庙里，在那里被捕。我没有听到巡捕要求人群解散。我没有参加集会。
    张海皇（Chang Hai Hwang，音译）说：我对骚乱一无所知。下午4点30分我出去买食物。我看到一群人。我出去看发生了什么事，结果被捕。我对篱笆的事一无所知。
    刘永典（Lau Yoong Dien，音译）说：骚乱期间我不在场。我在庙里买甘蔗时被捕。我没有参加集会。我对篱笆的事一无所知。

Tsang Tuh San fined $100 or three months imprisonment and
to put up a bond not do this sort of thing again.
Kao Yu Dien fined $80 or 70 days imprisonment and to put
up a bond not to do this sort of thing again.
Sung Yoong Li and Dong Tuh Dah fined $50 or 40 days
imprisonment and each to put up a bond not to do this sort of
thing again.
All the other accused fined $5 each or five days imprisonment.

Laing Sung Nyi (梁双喜), 26, coolie, Doo Tah Yui (涂發雲)
29, coolie, and Wong Kyih Zung (王吉成) 25, coolie, were then
brought into Court and charged as follows:-
For that they were concerned together on February 24,
1925, at Shanghai by means of threats and violence
did attempt to prevent the mill workers of the Nagai
Wata Kaisha Company No. 9 Mill situate at Markham
Road from continuing their work which they had a
legal right to do thereby interfering with the workers
of the said company, contrary to Article 223 of the
Chinese Provisional Criminal Code.
Det. Sergt. Andrews called, said:- On the morning of the 4th
Chinese detectives arrested the three men. I questioned them.
The first accused said he was a native of Chekiang and lived in
Yang Woo Lee, and came out last year to work at the China-Japan
Cotton Mill. At a meeting in Chapel, one Tsang Yoong Loong
gave him a badge and told him to station himself in the vicinity
of No. 9 mill and to stop labourers from going in. He admitted
having attended meetings in Chapel on the first day of the strike.
The second accused said that he came here three years ago
and was employed in a hemp factory on Robison Road, and afterwards
he went to work in the No. 7 Mill. He received instructions from
Wong Kyih Zung, the 3rd accused, to proceed to the mill to prevent
labourers from going to work. He admitted the offence.
The third accused said he came here four years ago and worked
in No. 5 Mill, and later went to the Doong Shing Mill. He denies
the offence. However, he was overheard trying to intimidate three
male workers. He says he does not know the second accused.
C.D.C. Zung Kwung Fung (        ) xxxxx called, said: I
arrested the first accused. I was disguised and had a basket.
Two women were ahead of me. The first and second accused stopped
me and asked me where I was going. I told them I was going to
the mill. They said," You must not go to work. If you do you
will be assaulted." I then arrested both men.
Chang Ah Nyi (張阿二), a detective employed at the mill,

宋永利（Sung Yoong Li，音译）和董德达（Dong Tuh Dah）各被罚款50元或监禁40天，并各自具保不再从事此类行为。
所有其他被告各被罚款5元或监禁五天。

梁双喜（Laing Sung Nyi），26岁，苦力；涂發雲（Doo Tah Yui），29岁，苦力；王吉成（Wong Kyih Zung），25岁，苦力，随后被带上法庭，指控如下：
指控他们于1925年2月24日在上海，通过威胁和暴力手段，企图阻止位于马克姆路（Markham Road）的长崎棉业株式会社（Nagai Wata Kaisha Company）第九纱厂的工人继续其拥有合法权利从事的工作，从而干扰了该公司的工人，此举违反《中华民国暂行新刑律》第223条。
警佐安德鲁斯（Det. Sergt. Andrews）出庭作证说：4日上午，中国侦探逮捕了这三名男子。我对他们进行了讯问。第一名被告说他是浙江人，住在杨伍李（Yang Woo Lee，音译），去年出来在中日纱厂工作。在教堂的一次集会上，一个叫张永龙（Tsang Yoong Loong，音译）的人给了他一枚徽章，并让他在第九纱厂附近驻守，阻止工人进入。他承认在罢工第一天参加了教堂的集会。
第二名被告说他三年前来到这里，受雇于罗宾森路（Robison Road）的一家麻纺厂，后来他去第七纱厂工作。他接到第三名被告王吉成的指示，前往纱厂阻止工人上班。他承认了罪行。
第三名被告说他四年前来到这里，在第五纱厂工作，后来去了东兴纱厂（Doong Shing Mill）。他否认有罪。然而，有人听到他试图恐吓三名男工。他说他不认识第二名被告。
刑事侦缉处长钟光凤（C.D.C. Zung Kwung Fung，音译）(        ) xxxxx 出庭作证说：我逮捕了第一名被告。我当时化了装，提着一个篮子。前面有两名妇女。第一和第二名被告拦住我，问我要去哪里。我说我要去纱厂。他们说：“你不准去上班。如果你去，就会遭到殴打。”于是我逮捕了这两个人。
张阿二（Chang Ah Nyi），一名受雇于纱厂的侦探，

said: I arrested the third accused. He was preventing labourers
from going to work. He was saying, " We are all Chinse and we
must be of one mind. If you go to work you will be assaulted."
He said this to about ten female workers. The women stopped
going to the mill.
This was the case for the prosecution.
In answer to the magistrate, the first accused, Laing Sung
Nyi, said: The badges were given to me by Chang Ying Loong. I
cannot read. He told me to keep them on my person. How can I alone
intimidate over 100 workers! I did not tell them not to go to
work.
Doo Tah Yui, the second accused, said: I passed the night
in Chapel. I did not tell the workers not to go to work. I was
passing the place at the time. The mill had not opened yet.
Wong Kyih Zung, the third accused, said: I did not prevent
anybody from going to work. I do not know why I was arrested.
I was told that a strike was on. I have been four years with the
Tung Shing Mill.
Mr. Covey, addressing the Court on behalf of the accused:
said, "If the Court finds them guilty, I ask that they be dealt
with as leniently as possible and to give them another chance."
Mr. Maitland: I have nothing to say to this.

Laing Sung Nyi was fined $20 or two weeks' imprisonment;
and Doo Tah Yui and Wong Kyih Zung were fined $10 each or one
week's imprisonment.

The Court announced that it would sit at 9 a.m. sharp on
Saturday, March 14, to hear the rest of the cases.

The Court then rose, the hour then being 7.45 p.m.

说：我逮捕了第三名被告。他正在阻止工人上班。他说：“我们都是中国人，必须同心协力。如果你去上班，就会遭到殴打。”他对大约十名女工说了这话。那些妇女便停止前往纱厂。
这是控方的案情陈述。
回答法官的提问时，第一名被告梁双喜说：徽章是张英龙（Chang Ying Loong，音译）给我的。我不识字。他让我把徽章带在身上。我一个人怎么能恐吓一百多名工人！我没有告诉他们不要去上班。
第二名被告涂發雲说：我在教堂过了一夜。我没有告诉工人不要去上班。当时我正路过那里。纱厂还没有开门。
第三名被告王吉成说：我没有阻止任何人去上班。我不知道为什么被捕。有人告诉我正在罢工。我在东兴纱厂已经四年了。
科维先生（Mr. Covey）代表被告向法庭陈述说：“如果法庭判定他们有罪，我请求尽可能从轻处理，给他们一次改过自新的机会。”
梅特兰先生（Mr. Maitland）：我对此无话可说。

梁双喜被罚款20元或监禁两周；涂發雲和王吉成各被罚款10元或监禁一周。

法庭宣布将于3月14日星期六上午9时整开庭，审理其余案件。

法庭随即休庭，当时时间为晚上7点45分。

您的顺从仆人，
文书助理。

刑事侦缉处长。

关于日本领事馆提供的与罢工有关的嫌疑地址及人员的报告。

由 D. I. Givens 撰写，转呈

先生：

经查询，霞飞路宝康里54号现由一名朝鲜人居住，该人在上海电车公司担任稽查员。

Summary Translation of the Regulations Governing Tung
Fu Huh Tsoh Shae(同学合作社) which existed during the
years 1922-1923 no. 326-120 Paoshan Road, near Heng Pang
Jiao, Chapei, and whose promoter named Tong Shun Lee
(唐仲禮), a native of Quinsan and an employee in the
Lithographic Department of the Commercial Press, Ltd(Works),
aged about 35, still lives in the upstairs of that house,
the downstair room being occupied by a grocer's shop trading
under the name Tai Lai Fung(泰來豐):
------------------
1. Aim: With a view to mutual assistance, this shop deals in
provisions and sundry articles necessary for daily use at
very reasonable prices, while its profits are equally
divided among the shareholders.
2. Name: Tung Fu Huh Tsoh Shae(同学合作社), Consumption
Department.
3. Capital: Amount indefinite, but each share is sold at $5.00.
4. Members: Any one desiring to subscribe may become a member
and all are cordially welcomed.
5. Payment: Payment of shares may be either made at the time of
purchase or in instalments within 6 months against receipt.
6. Fee for membership: $1.00 from each member is collected as
fee for membership, which will be utilized for buying
furniture, etc.
7. Limit of shares: No member will be permitted to purchase
more than 10 shares, or to have the right to more than one
vote.
8. Interest: 8 per cent interest will be allowed on all shares.
9. Bonds: An order book will be issued to each member in which
the amount of his shares will be entered and properly signed
and chopped by the manger and the accountant in acknowledgment
on a specified page.
10. Compass: The business is started in rice, firewood, beanoil,

REPORT ON labour movements in Chapel

Made by Tan Shao-liang Forwarded by
Clerical Assistant

Sir,
Between 2 to 5 p.m. on February 26 about 700 cotton
mill workers from Gordon and Pootoo Road districts called
at the Western District Labour Club 滬西工友俱樂部 in the Jan Tsh
Lee 三德里 alleyway behind the Ta Foong Cotton Mill
Tae Tsz Wei 潭子灣 Chapel when twenty cents was paid to
each one able to present a mill work book. Owing to the
large number of workers present, payment was made at three
different addresses, viz in houses Nos. 1, 24 and 57 in
the same alleyway. Three men were engaged at each of
these places: one examining the books, another taking a
record of the names and the third handing out the money.
The recipients were told not to resume work notwithstanding
the negotiations going on at the Chinese Chamber of Commerce.

Sir,

I beg to report that at 1 p.m. February 27 two bobbed
hair girl students, one of about 26 years of age and the other
about 21 called at the Western District Labour Club 沪西工友俱乐部
No1 San Teh Lee behind the Ta Foong Cotton Mill, Tae Tsz Wei
Chapel, where about 100 cotton mill workers were gathered.
They (the girl students) declared that the men arrested
and taken into custody by the Chinese Police in connection
with the strike would be released to-day (February 28) whilst
those in the custody of the Settlement Police will be set
at liberty the day after; they add that the family of each
prisoner could obtain $2.00 from them (the girl students)
to buy food for them after their release. About ten
persons representing themselves as members of the prisoners'
families then received this gratuity. The girl students
left at 2 p.m.

At 3 p.m. two men at No.24 San Teh Lee commenced
paying out 20 cents each to about 70 persons claiming to be
workers of the Nikka Cotton Mill. They also distributed
a circular (copy attached) which states "An agreement
(? for the settlement of the strike) has been signed and
labourers will resume work. On Sunday March 1 (?February 28) a mass
meeting will be held at Pang Peh (Chapel) and all should
come to listen to the conditions (of the agreement)."

At this stage a Sergeant and three Constables from
the Chapel Police arrived on bicycles and warned the crowd

March 2 1925

REPORT ON a mass meeting held in Chapei on March 1, 1925.

Made by Tan Shao-liang Forwarded by Director of Criminal Investigation
Clerical assistant.

Sir,

At 3 p.m. on Sunday (March 1) a mass meeting of cotton
mill workers was held on a piece of vacant ground in the
rear of San Teh Lee 三德里 Tae Tsz Wei, Chapei when about
600 men and women were present.

The first speaker was Li Say Ching 李瑞清 representative
of the Nikka Cotton Mill workers, who said that the meeting
had been called to celebrate the victory of the workers and
the signature by the Japanese of the agreement granting
their demands. He thanked the Chinese Chamber of Commerce
and the Chinese Police for assistance and cooperation
rendered to the workers in effecting a settlement.
He added that the workers of the Naigai, the Nikka, the
Dong Shing and the Toyoda Cotton Mills have already formed
an association of their own but they should combine to
form a General Union and to establish a free school and
hospital for workers who should contribute according to
their means towards their maintenance.

Pae Tung Ling, Chairman of the Boone Road Street Union,
was then elected President of the Cotton Mill Workers
Federation. In the course of his address he said, "If the
Japanese illtreat you the next time, you need not return
the insult by starting a riot neither by assaulting the
Japanese, but you should simply go on strike which is
the best method of resistance.".

A bobbed hair girl student of about 21 years of age

由谭绍良撰写，由刑事侦缉处处长转呈

先生：

周日（3月1日）下午3时，在闸北潭子湾三德里背后的一块空地上举行了棉纺厂工人群众集会，约有600名男女出席。

第一位发言者是李瑞清，日华纱厂工人代表，他说召开此次会议是为了庆祝工人的胜利以及日本人签署满足其要求的协议。他感谢中国商会和中国警察在促成和解方面向工人提供的协助与合作。他补充说，内外棉、日华、东华和丰田纱厂的工人已经组成了各自的协会，但他们应该联合起来组成一个总工会，并为工人建立免费学校和医院，工人应根据其能力出资维持这些机构。

随后，博恩路街道联合会主席潘冬林当选为棉纺厂工人联合会主席。他在讲话中说：“如果日本人下次再虐待你们，你们不必通过发动暴乱或袭击日本人来回击侮辱，而应该仅仅进行罢工，这是最好的抵抗方法。”

Rough translation of the attached circular.

Regulations of the Association of Workers in the Nagai Cotton
Mills.

Art. 1 NAME. Only workers of the above mills may participate
in the formation of the above organisation.
Hence the name.

Art. 2. OBJECT. It will be the object of the Association
to protect the privileges and rights of the
workers.

Art. 3. MEMBERS. Workers of the above mills may be admitted
as members.

Art. 4 DUTIES. The duties of the Association shall be:-
(a) to organise an "Insurance" against loss
of employment.
(b) to organise an Employment agency.
(c) to form a Mutual aid association in case
of death, wounding or illness.
(d) to establish a free hospital
(e) to open a free school for workers and
their children.
(f) to establish a Mutual Cooperation bureau (?)
(g) to form a Club
(h) to open a Reading Room
(i) to deliver lectures
(j) to carry out anything that will prove
beneficial to workers.

Art. 5 ORGANISATION.(a) Workers in each Department of the Mills
shall elect a Committee of 3 to 5 persons
or every 10 workers should elect one
representative and ten representatives to
form a Committee.
pages.zh:
所附传单的粗略译文。

内外棉纱厂工人协会章程。

第1条 名称。只有上述纱厂的工人方可参与组建上述组织。
故以此命名。

第2条 宗旨。本协会的宗旨是保护工人的特权和权利。

第3条 会员。上述纱厂的工人可被接纳为会员。

第4条 职责。本协会的职责应为：-
(a) 组织针对失业损失的“保险”。
(b) 组织职业介绍所。
(c) 在死亡、受伤或生病时成立互助协会。
(d) 建立免费医院
(e) 为工人及其子女开设免费学校。
(f) 建立互助合作局 (?)
(g) 组建俱乐部
(h) 开设阅览室
(i) 举办讲座
(j) 开展任何对工人有益的事情。

第5条 组织。(a) 纱厂各部门的工人应选举一个由3至5人组成的委员会，或者每10名工人选举一名代表，由十名代表组成一个委员会。

Art. 9. Members committing the following offences

the Chinese authorities, that they are anxious to

when the latter find the hands at work in the mills.

The following are extracts from the Shanghai Nippo

The Shanghai Nippo.

SUPPLY OF FUNDS FROM THE DAH HWO (大夏) COLLEGE
THROUGH COCOON DEALERS ASSOCIATION.

It is now known that the supporters of the
present disturbance are Russian Communists. The Dah Hwo
College which is an organ of the Russian Communists
and controlled by Karakhan, has, it is said, supplied
funds to the agitators to cover their expenses.

THE UNION OF SHANGHAI COTTON MILLS' TELEGRAPHS
TO MINISTER OF FOREIGN DEPARTMENT.

It is plain that the agitators in the
present disturbance are the agents of Russian
Communists. It is a serious matter that Russia has
ignored the friendship between Japan and Russia which
has lately been restored. We sincerely hope that our
Government will negotiate with the Russians concerned
and stop the disturbances.
The Japanese Chamber of Commerce, Shanghai,
has sent a telegram couched in these terms to the
Japanese Minister at Peking.

The Shanghai Nichi Nichi.

Osaka, February 18.

A conference was held at the Osaka Hotel
to-day, and it was decided that Mr. Kita of the Nikka
Boseki, Mr. Kodama of the Shanghai Boseki, Mr. Fukumoto

in the cotton mills in Shanghai as a common dispute

agitators who are not workmen, carrying weapons
raided the mills and injured some Japanese. We
believe that the disturbance cannot be settled in
an ordinary way. The Government should negotiate
with the Chinese Government for the arrest of the
agitators and intimidators to settle the disturbance
at once, and to take measures to secure compensation

Translation from the "Shanghai Nippo." February 18, 1925.

At the meeting of the Japanese Chamber of Commerce, the following resolution was passed in connection with the strike of workers in the Japanese Mills:-

"Judging by the developments that have taken place in the strike amongst workers in the Japanese Cotton Mills in Shanghai, it is hardly believable that the present boycott has anything to do with ordinary labour problems. Persons other than workers, such as fiery rowdies etc. have been noticed rushing into factories tampering and causing serious damage to the machinery, whilst some have armed themselves with dangerous weapons and attacked Japanese with serious results.

"The affair cannot be settled by ordinary measures and therefore the Home Government should be requested to instruct the Ministry for Foreign Affairs to lodge a strong protest against the Chinese Government and to urge for the arrest of the agitators and to maintain a strict watch over them. The Chinese Government should also be approached for the payment of compensation to the satisfaction of the Japanese Government for all damage to property and person, and to bring about a prompt settlement of the unfortunate incident. The Japanese Government should be requested, if necessary, to act according to circumstances and with determination."

在日本商会会议上，就日本纱厂工人罢工一事通过了以下决议：-

“鉴于上海日本棉纺厂工人罢工事态的发展，很难相信目前的抵制行动与普通劳工问题有关。人们注意到，除工人以外的其他人，如激烈的暴徒等，冲入工厂，篡改并严重损坏机器，而有些人则持有危险武器攻击日本人，造成严重后果。

“此事无法通过常规措施解决，因此应请求本国政府指示外务省向中国政府提出强烈抗议，并要求逮捕煽动者并对其严加监视。还应与中国政府交涉，要求其对所有财产和人身损害支付令日本政府满意的赔偿，并促使这一不幸事件得到迅速解决。如有必要，应请求日本政府根据情况果断采取行动。”

"to suppress the strikers. We have neither money nor
"influence. We depend only on our firm attitude. We
"must take revenge if our movement fails. The day will
"come when the Japanese capitalism will be overthrown."

20 cents each as an encouragement to carry on the strike.

them sat beside a table in the office of the Union. He

Sir,
I beg to report that between 2 to 4 p.m. February 25
about 200 mill strikers gathered near the Ta Foong Mill
at Tae Tsz Wei, Chapel. The man Zou was again present
He addressed them as follows:- "D'ont worry about your
wages. You will be paid in big money if we succeed in
settling the matter with the Japanese."
The attached circular was distributed by him amongst
those who were present. It reads, in part, as follows:-
"The Japanese capitalists broke their promise yesterday
"when they told the mediators, the Fu Yi Mill, that
"they would not discuss terms until next Tuesday.
"They have insulted us and they are not sincere.
"This is because they are wealthy and can depend on
"the running dogs, the Settlement and Chinese Police,
"to suppress the strikers. We have neither money nor
"influence. We depend only on our firm attitude. We
"must take revenge if our movement fails. The day will
"come when the Japanese capitalism will be overthrown."
At 4 p.m. a man from the Labour Union at San Teh Lee
Tae Tsz Wei invited the strikers to go in and receive
20 cents each as an encouragement to carry on the strike.
About 100 workers called and received payment, they being
required to produced books issued by mills formerly
employing them, as a sign of good faith. The man who paid
them sat beside a table in the office of the Union. He

Shanghai, February 17, 1925.

Sir,

Further to the repeated representations made
to you relative to the activities of strike promoters
on the northern side of the Soochow Creek in Chinese
territory, west of Markham Road, I have the honour to
bring to your notice that reports reaching me indicate
that the demonstration of agitators on February 16 were
as bad if not worse than on any previous day. These
reports show that on the afternoon of the date in
quest large pickets of agitators carrying several
inscribed flags assembled at the jetties on the Soochow
Creek used by workers and scrutinized everybody that
passed. The crowds appeared to be most active at the
jetties opposite Mill No. 9, No. 60 Markham Road,
and at the landing leading near the Dah Foong
Cotton Mill. The Municipal Police are convinced
that this campaign of intimidation is largely
responsible for the prolongation of the strike, and
hope that effective measures will be taken to bring it
to an end. In this connection, the following list
of names of persons known to be leaders in the agitation
may be useful to you:

Sir,

Made by D. S. Douglas Forwarded by [Signature].

Sir,

I beg to report that at 2 p.m. Feb. 19th '25,
accompanied by L.C. of W.T. Ware, and C.D.C.s To Lim, Tuk
and So Tan Piao, I went to the Chinese Police Station at
Ying Ziang Kong (引翔港), with a warrant for the arrest
of four of the ringleaders of the cotton mill strikers in
the Yangtszepoo district. At the said Police Station, arrange-
ments had been made for three of the men named in the warrant
to meet us there, but only one of them, named "Tsha Ts'ao
(曹子草), turned up.

The above party waited at the Station for some
time before placing Tsha Ts'ao under arrest, and efforts
were made to get the other persons named in the warrant to
come to the Station, also, but none of them came.

About 1.45 p.m. Tsha Ts'ao was informed that
there was a warrant for his arrest, and after being questioned
by the Inspector in charge of Ying Ziang Kong Chinese Police
Station, he was placed in the cells. Apparently, news of
the arrest of Tsha Ts'ao reached a number of the strikers,
who were at that time holding a meeting in a field near Tseu
Ka Wei Village (周家渡), which is about 1 li north of
Ying Ziang Kong. At 3 p.m. about 700 strikers assembled
outside the Police Station, and demanded the release of the
arrested man.

The mob remained outside the fence in front of
the Station, but on seeing Sergt. Ware and myself at the
Station door, a number of them shouted that there were foreign

上述人员在将曹子草逮捕前，在巡捕房等待了一段时间，并努力让逮捕令上列名的其他人也来到巡捕房，但他们均未前来。

car and go to Yangtszepoo Station for assistance.

Inspector Johnston, D.S. Grabb and a squad of
Sikhs arrived on the scene at 5.30 p.m., and co-operated
with the Chinese Police. The mob were ordered to disperse
by Inspector Johnston, or they would be fired on, but their
ringleaders, named Zung Tsch san and Hau Yu Hien told
them not to move, they ( the ringleaders ) were arrested,
and the Settlement squad of police charged the crowd, whilst
the Chinese Police opened fire and fired volley after volley
over their heads.

Made by D.S. Douglas. Forwarded by Inspector, Johnstone.

Sir,

I beg to forward herewith a report on the labour
unrest in this district during the month of February 1925.

(1) Previous to the strike, which commenced in
this district on Feb. 24th 1925, many of the workers used to meet
at the Workers' School and Union at No.603 Heichow Road. At
this address, the workers used to meet for the supposed purpose
of being taught to read and write. The only connection which
the School and Union has with any other institution, is the
fact that a female teacher of the school, named Woo Sion Tsin
(吴先清), who took a leading part in the strike was previously
employed at the Ning-shao Public School (寧紹公學), North
Szechuen Road Extension, near Wang Poo Bridge (橫浜桥). Woo
Sion Tsin was released on $100.- bail, which was put up by
one Wong Sin Yui (汪黃雪源), the school master of the Ning-shao
School.

A man named Zung Tseh San (陳竹山), who is now
in custody in connection with the strike, and who was previous
to the strike, employed as a door keeper at No.603 Heichow Road,
by the Workers' School and Union, was according to information
received, seen on a number of occasions taking a leading part
among the strikers in the Western District, and it is believed
that the Workers' School and Union at No.603 Heichow Road was
connected with the Nagai Wata Kaisha Workers' Union at Agbison
Road.

the Nagai Wata Kaisha in Pootoo Road District, but originated

    (8) At the Dah Kong Mill, the trouble lasted 11
days, from Feb. 14th to 25th and at the Yue Fong Hill, the trouble
lasted 8 days, from Feb. 18th to 26th.
    (9) As the strike became prolonged, the majority of
the strikers seemed disposed to return to work.
    (10) Police were posted at all mills to prevent
damage being done by the strikers. The strikers were kept on
the move and not allowed to hold meetings. All the leaders and
agitators who could be located were arrested and charged and
warrants were issued against those, whose names were known, but
who could not be located. The action of the Police had the effect
of preserving order in the Settlement, as no demonstrations
of a disorderly nature occurred, with the exception of a riot
at Ying Ziao Hong, on the borders of the Settlement, which
followed the arrest of the leader of the strikers, but the mob
was dispersed and 16 arrests made.
    (11) No damage was done to any buildings or machinery
by the strikers.
    (12) The financial loss by the Dah Kong Mill is
estimated at $25,000 and the financial loss of the Yue Fong
Mill is estimated at $13,000.

I beg to report that the Dah Kong Cotton Mill

No.96 East Yangtsepoo Road are now working quite peacefully,
and practically, all the workers have resumed work.

On Feb. 27th, information was received about
one, Yui Foo Liang (郁南良), who is a cadre foreman,
employed at the Dah Kong Mill having been active in intimi-
dating a number of workers at the quarters of the said mill,
on the evening of Feb. 26th. According to our information,
this man paid 20 cents to each worker, who promised not to
resume work. At 4 p.m. Feb. 27th, Yui Foo Liang was located
at his home in Yang Ka Pai (杨家宅) village off Pingyang
Road, and was arrested and charged with acting as a
ringleader in a strike. He will be taken before the Mixed
Court to-day (28/2/30).

distribute them. Inquiries were made at the said address,

on File at this Station since Feb. 18th. Tseu Ah Doo was

Sir,
The encouragement given by Loh Dung of the Yue Fong Cotton Mill not to resume was couched in rather ambiguous language. It proves that he behaved incorrectly, but the evidence is not sufficient to sustain a charge.
It would be impossible to do much until the police get further evidence, but it is desirable in the meantime to keep a watch on Loh Dung (陸純).
I am, Sir,

Made by D.C. Douglas Forwarded by [Signature]

Sir,

With reference to the strike of cotton mill workers in this district, I beg to report that a comparatively small number of workers employed at the Yue Fong Cotton Mill (裕豐紗廠) returned to work on Feb. 25th and 26th after the said mill resumed work.

During the strike, the No. 1 Interpreter, employed at the Yue Fong Mill, named Loh Dung (陸□), has remained at work and has apparently given the mill manager to believe that he is assisting him to settle the strike, when on the other hand, he has been encouraging the workers not to resume work.

On Feb. 24th 1925, from 2 to 5.30 p.m. a meeting attended by 30 foremen and 120 women was held in the dining room at the said mill. The meeting was addressed by Loh Dung, who was present to represent the manager of the mill, and he encouraged the workers not to resume work until the persons arrested in connection with the strike had been released. Two Chinese detectives, who were instructed by me to attend the meeting heard Loh make a statement to that effect. A statement has been taken from both detectives who attended the meeting and are attached herewith.

At about 5.30 p.m. Feb. 25th '25, the Director of Criminal Intelligence and myself interviewed the manager of the Yue Fong Mill and informed him of what Loh Dung had said at the meeting and also that information

REPORT OF POLICE INVESTIGATIONS.

The following is the statement of C.D.C.67 Ng Zang Khe
native of _________________________ taken by me D. S. Douglas
at Y'poo Station on the Feb. 26th '25 and interpreted by Interpreter Kung

On Feb. 24th 1925, I was instructed by D. S.
Douglas to go to the Yue Fong Cotton Mill (裕豐紗廠) at No.98
East Yangtszepoo Road together with C.D.C.107 Wong Kwe Yoong
for the purpose of attending a meeting of the foremen and women
employed at the mill, who held a meeting there at 2 p.m. on
the said date. The meeting was addressed by one , Loh Dung
(陸 杜 ), who is employed as No.1 Interpreter at the mill.
He stated that he thought the workers were on strike in sympathy
with the workers of the Naigai Wata Kaisha Mills. "But that
the conditions of the Yue Fong Mill are quite good," he said,
"Why don't you resume work ? Is it because you want to wait
until the Naigai Wata Kaisha Mills resume work? If you want
an increase of wages, I will negotiate with the Japanese manager
about it. Perhaps you only want to resume work after the
release of those in custody in connection with the strike. I
will talk to the Japanese manager and ask him to request the
Police to release the men in custody, but I cannot guarantee
their release. Those who demand the release of the men in
custody before resuming work, stand up." All the workers
stood up.

In the course of my inquiries in connection
with the strike, I have heard many of the workers say that
Loh Dung was responsible for the workers not returning to duty
but I have been unable to get any of them to come forward and
give evidence to this effect.

Signed Ng Zang Khe.

No.14 The Strikers' Press Feb. 25th 1925.
Published by the Nagai Wata Kaisha Cotton Mill Labourers Union.

Workers hold their righteousness.
Labourers' organisations in other districts give help.

It has been half a month since we struck
work. The news of the strike have spread throughout China. The
labourers of other districts, on hearing the ill-treatment of the
Japanese, sympathize with us and are willing to help us by raising
漢冶萍總
funds, in order that we can gain success. The Han Yih Ping La-
工 會 鄭州全國鐵路總工會
bourers'Association, the Chungchow National Railway Labourers'
海員工會 杭州青年勞工
Association, the Sailors'Association, the Young Labourers'
協 會
Association of Hangchow, and many other labourers organisations
have either wired or sent letters to us, stating that they wish to
do their best to help us. They are going to raise funds, which
they will forward to us to support us in the strike. Fellow-
workers! With the help of so many organisations, we ought to be
more closely united and maintain to the end till we gain the victory.

We are not cheated by the Japanese.

The Japanese capitalists have apparently become
embarrassed as we do not resume work, so they are going to entice us
to work by stating that if we go to report for work, we shall receive
our wages. Several workers went to report for work, but they found
that they were cheated, as they were not paid. Now we have seen
the trick, so nobody would go to the mills again.

Funds raised in Shanghai, to be distributed by
Workers' Union.
恒 豐 鴻 益
The Heng Fong and Foo Yih Cotton Mills have raised
funds to support us. It is learned that money has already been
received from them and is soon to be distributed to us by the Workers'
Union. We shall not be short of money for several days to come, so
we must not resume work until the signatures of the Japanese capitalists
are obtained.

工人坚持正义。
其他地区劳工组织给予援助。

我们罢工已半月有余。罢工消息传遍全中国。其他地区的劳工听闻日本人的虐待行径，对我们深表同情，并愿意通过筹集汉冶萍总工会资金来帮助我们，以期我们获得成功。汉冶萍总工会、郑州全国铁路总工会、海员工会、杭州青年劳工协会以及许多其他劳工组织，均已致电或致函我们，表示愿尽全力相助。他们将筹集资金并汇给我们，以支持我们的罢工。工友们！在如此多组织的帮助下，我们应当更加紧密地团结在一起，坚持到底，直至取得胜利。

我们不再受日本人欺骗。

由于我们未复工，日本资本家显然已陷入困境，因此他们试图诱骗我们复工，声称若去报到上班，便可领取工资。几名工人前去报到，却发现受骗，因为他们并未领到工资。如今我们已识破其诡计，故无人再前往工厂。

上海筹集的资金，将由工会分发。
恒丰、鸿益两棉纺厂已筹集资金支持我们。据悉，款项已从该两厂收到，不久将由工会分发给我们。未来数日我们将不缺资金，因此在获得日本资本家的签字承诺之前，我们绝不复工。

Feb. 25th 1925.

Further REPORT ON Strike of Cotton Mill Workers in this District.

Made by D. C. Douglas. Forwarded by Mcpherson Johnson.

Sir,

I beg to report that the two cotton mills in this district affected by the strike partially resume work this morning (25-2-25). At the Dah Hong (大康) Cotton Mill, at No. 2 Tangyuch Road 1200 workers turned up for work, but only 286 turned up for work at the Yu Fong (裕豐) Cotton Mill, at No. 98 East Yangtsepoo Road, but it is expected that a bigger number will turn up for work on Feb. 26th, as it is believed that news of the mill intending to resume work has not reached the out-lying districts, where many of the workers reside.

On Feb. 24th, the managers of both the above mentioned mills received letters, both of which are attached to this report.

At about 9 p.m. Feb. 24th, information was received at this Station about one Tsang Ah San (張阿三), a coolie, employed at the Dah Hong Mill having been active in intimidating workers of that mill. This man was arrested at the mill quarters and has been charged with being a leader in a strike. He will be taken before the Mixed Court to-day (25-2-25) and a remand for the Japanese Assessor applied for.

Every effort is being made to trace and arrest all agitators and precautions are being taken to prevent picketing by the strikers.

I am, Sir,
Yours obediently,
James Douglas.
D. S.

D. C. I.

关于本区棉纺厂工人罢工的进一步报告。

由 D. C. Douglas 撰写。由 Mcpherson Johnson 转呈。

先生：

谨此报告，本区受罢工影响的两家棉纺厂于今日上午（1925年2月25日）部分复工。位于唐玉路2号的大康（Dah Hong）棉纺厂有1200名工人到岗上班，但位于杨树浦路东段98号的裕丰（Yu Fong）棉纺厂仅有286名工人到岗。预计2月26日到岗人数将会增加，因为据信打算复工的消息尚未传至许多工人居住的偏远地区。

2月24日，上述两家工厂的经理均收到信件，这两封信件均附于本报告之后。

2月24日晚9时许，本巡捕房接到情报，称受雇于大康厂的苦力张阿三（Tsang Ah San）积极恐吓该厂工人。此人已在厂区宿舍被捕，并被指控为罢工领袖。他将于今日（1925年2月25日）被提解至会审公廨，并将申请由日本陪审员参与延期审理。

正全力追查并逮捕所有煽动者，同时采取预防措施以防止罢工者纠察。

此致，
敬礼，
James Douglas。
副巡官。

副总督察。

To the Manager,
    Dah Kong Cotton Mill.

Sir,

    Since the commencement of the strike,
no settlement has as yet been reached between both parties.
We learn from the workers of various departments, that
the management, not only reject their demands, but bribe
the Police of both the Settlement and Chinese territories,
so their grievance cannot be redressed. They have decided
to damage the machines in the mill, as soon as they resume
work.

    We, on hearing this, have to inform you of
what they are to do . If you open your mill before a settle-
ment is reached, and have your machines destroyed, we would
take no responsibility for this.

                The heads of various depart-
                ments of the mill.

先生：

自罢工开始以来，双方迄今未达成和解。我们从各部门工人处获悉，资方不仅拒绝他们的要求，还贿赂租界及华界的警察，致使他们的冤屈无法伸张。他们决定一旦复工，便破坏厂内机器。

Yue Yong Cotton Mill.
Sirs,

It has been ten days since the strike
began on the 14th inst, but no settlement has as yet
been reached between both parties. We learn from the
workers of various departments that the management, not
only reject their demands, but bribe the police of both
the Settlement and Chinese territories, so their grievance
cannot be redressed. They have decided to damage the
machines in the mill, as soon as they resume work.

We, on hearing this, have to inform
you of what they are to do. If you open your mill
before a settlement is reached, and have your machines
destroyed, we would take no responsibility for this.

The heads of various depart-
ments of Nos. 1 and 2 mills.

Sir,

No meetings were held by the strikers on Feb. 22nd, and the district is more quiet and all the mills, with the exception of the two above mentioned, are working quite peacefully.

Attached herewith are copies of pamphlets which were siezed at the strikers headquarters at Tseu Kai Wei (周家嘴) Village on Feb. 20th.

formed a Strike Support Society, calling all the Chinese
to help us. We ought to be more unanimous than before.

Fellow-workers! We work in the Japanese owned Mills.
The Japanese look upon us as cows and horses. They beat or
swear at us as they like. We are all Chinese, when we are
illtreated by the Japanese, it is not only the disgrace of us
workers, but also that of the 400,000,000 people of the nation.
Fellow workers! We ought to be of one mind and protest against
the cruelty of the Japanese. We have been acting as cows and
horses, but hereafter, we shall act as men, in order to save
the face of us workers, as well as the prestige of all the
Chinese. The Chinese employees of the 11 mills of Naigai Wata
Kaisha, have all gone on strike, followed by those of the China
Japan Mills and Toyoda Mills. They are doing the right.
Fellow worker! We shall be all of one mind and unite to protest
against the illtreatment of the Japanese. We shall listen to
what the Labourers' Association says, and when we take the
instructions of the Association, we are of the same mind and
can gain our last victory.

The Dah Hong Cotton Mill Labour
Association.

工友们！我们在日本拥有的纱厂工作。
日本人视我们如牛马。他们随意殴打或
辱骂我们。我们都是中国人，当我们受到
日本人虐待时，这不仅是我们
工人的耻辱，也是全国四亿人民的耻辱。
工友们！我们应当同心协力，抗议
日本人的暴行。我们过去像牛马一样行事，但从今以后，我们将像人一样行事，以保全我们工人的脸面，以及所有
中国人的尊严。内外棉株式会社（Naigai Wata Kaisha）旗下11家纱厂的中国雇员已全部罢工，随后华日纱厂（China Japan Mills）和丰田纱厂（Toyoda Mills）的工人也相继罢工。他们的做法是正确的。
工友！我们要万众一心，联合起来抗议
日本人的虐待。我们要听从劳工协会的指示，当我们遵循
协会的指令时，我们便同心同德，
并能取得最终胜利。

大宏纱厂劳工
协会。

Japanese, foreign Police arrested some of our friends. Foreign Police
firing in the Chinese territory. China is really a 'dead nation'.
The Native Police, threatened and forced by the Japanese, could not
but arrest us for them. Now, all the Chinese in Shanghai have arisen
in a protest against the Japanese, and all the people in the country
are going to help us. So we ought to be more closely united and
maintain firmly to the end, then our victory is certain. Whoever
goes to work first is a surrenderor to the Japanese and a seller of
the country.

中国巡捕在日本人的威胁和强迫下，不得不

Feb. 21st 1925.

Further REPORT ON Strike of Cotton Mill Workers in this district.

Made by O. . Douglas Forwarded by Joseph Johnston.

Sir,
I beg to report that since the arrest of a number
of the cotton mill strike leaders in this district on Feb.
19th 1925, the strikers have not been so active. An attempt
was made to hold a meeting at Tsau Ka Wai (周家湾) Village
north of Ying Liang Kong (引翔港), at 8 a.m. on Feb. 20th
1925, but as the Chinese Police were on the scene prior to
that time no meeting was held. This meeting was to have been
addressed by Woo Sien Tsing (吴先清), a female teacher, who
was previously attached to the Workers' School and Union
at No. 605 Lieouhow Road.
On the evening of Feb. 20th, efforts were made by
detectives attached to this station to locate and arrest Woo
Sien Tsing, for whose arrest a warrant has been issued, but
she could not be located. It was learned by detectives who
made inquiries that Woo Sien Tsing had been assaulted by a
number of the strikers, which shows that the strikers are
loosing faith in their leaders. Efforts are still being made
to locate this woman as well as other strike leaders, whose
names are known to us.
The Dah Kong Cotton Mill (大康纱厂) situated at No. 2
Tengyueh Road still remains closed and at the Yue Fong Cotton
Mill (裕丰纱厂), situated at No. 98 East Yangtszepoo Road, only
about 200 turned up for the night shift at 6 p.m. on Feb. 20th
and a like number turned up for day shift at 6 a.m. Feb. 21st.
All the other mills in the district are working quite peace-
fully.

先生：
谨此报告，自1925年2月
19日本区多名棉厂罢工领袖被捕以来，罢工者的活动已不如先前活跃。曾有人试图于1925年2月20日上午8时在引翔港（Ying Liang Kong）以北的周家湾（Tsau Ka Wai）村举行集会，但由于中国警察在此之前已到达现场，集会未能举行。此次集会原定由吴先清（Woo Sien Tsing）女士发表演讲，她此前曾在柳州路605号的工人学校和工会任职。
2月20日晚，本巡捕房的侦探努力寻找并逮捕吴先清，当局已签发对其逮捕令，但未能找到其下落。经侦探调查得知，吴先清遭到数名罢工者的袭击，这表明罢工者正逐渐失去对领导人的信任。目前仍在努力寻找这名女子以及其他已知姓名的罢工领袖。
位于通州路2号的大康纱厂（Dah Kong Cotton Mill）仍然关闭，位于东杨树浦路98号的裕丰纱厂（Yue Fong Cotton Mill），在2月20日下午6点的夜班中仅有约200人到岗，2月21日上午6点的日班也有同样数量的人到岗。
本区所有其他工厂均在平稳运作。

Sir,

I beg to report that the Dah Kong Cotton Mill (大康紗廠), situated at No. 2 Tengyueh Road is still closed down. The Yue Fong Cotton Mill (裕豐紗廠) situated at No. 98 East Yangtszepoo Road has not yet been able to resume work, as only 250 employees turned up for work, for the night shift at 6 p.m. on Feb. 19th, and only 250 turned up for work at 6 a.m. on Feb. 20th. 6030

We work in the Japanese Mills and are in great
distress. Every day we work for 12 hours, during which period
we have no time for rest. Formerly, we had half an hour's time
for tiffin, but now we have only fifteen minutes. Night work
is more hard than day work. After one week's night work, our
faces turn sallow and become swollen. We work so hard for them
through the year and make for them profits, amounting to several
hundreds of million dollars. But the Japanese are so hard-hearted,
that our wages are not even sufficient for our necessary expenses,
owing to the daily increase in the value of things. Our wages are
not increased. The young and old are waiting at home for food, but
our wages are not enough for it. How poor we are! What is more oppressive
is the assault committed by the Japanese without reason. The Japanese
supervisors backed by the authorities given them by the Japanese
proprietors, treat us as though we were oxen and horses. We are
badly assaulted when we make the slightest mistake, and they swear
at us, saying 'slaves' etc. Sometimes, workers are so seriously
hurt by them about the head that blood flows from it, but they are
sent to the Police Station to be imprisoned. If somebody protests
against this, he is to be dismissed. Despite our insufficient
wages, the Japanese take any occasions to decrease them. If we
make a slight mistake, we shall be heavily fined. Formerly, our
wages were distributed every two weeks, but now it is prolonged to
3 or 4 weeks. We live on our wages, but the Japanese put them in
the bank for interest. The illtreatments of Japanese are numerous.
Formerly, those on day shift were rewarded $1.00, and those on night
shift, $1.30, if they did not once fail to be present for work between
the times of distributing wages. They did this in order to make us
work without interruption. But in fact, we deserved our rewards for
our hard work. They were only inveigling our ignorant workers by
calling them 'rewards'. Now, the rewards have been reduced to
pages.zh:
6030
29/2/25

我们在日本纱厂工作，处境
极为困苦。每天工作12小时，在此期间
我们没有休息时间。以前，我们有半小时
吃午饭的时间，但现在只有十五分钟。夜班
比白班更辛苦。上了一周夜班后，我们的
脸色变得蜡黄且浮肿。我们整年为他们如此
辛勤工作，为他们创造高达数
亿美元的利润。但日本人如此狠心，
由于物价每日上涨，我们的工资甚至不足以支付
必要开支。我们的工资没有增加。老小在家
等着吃饭，但我们的工资不够糊口。我们是多么贫穷啊！更令人压迫
的是日本人无故进行的殴打。日本
监工仗着日本业主赋予他们的权力，待我们
如牛马。只要我们稍有过失，就会遭到
严重殴打，他们还辱骂我们，叫我们“奴隶”等。有时，工人头部被他们打得
鲜血直流，但却被送到巡捕房监禁。如果有人对此
提出抗议，就会被解雇。尽管我们的工资
不足，日本人还找各种借口克扣。如果我们
犯一点小错，就会被重罚。以前，我们的工资
每两周发放一次，但现在延长到
3或4周。我们靠工资生活，但日本人却把工资存入银行赚取利息。日本人的虐待不胜枚举。
以前，如果在发薪期间全勤，白班工人奖励1.00元，夜班工人奖励1.30元。他们这样做是为了让我们不间断地工作。但实际上，这是我们辛勤工作应得的报酬。他们只是用“奖励”的名义来诱骗我们这些无知的工人。现在，奖励已减少为

pages.en:
bo cents. For our part we shall abide the Japanese capitalists
are really negotiable. If they promise to give us to the utmost,
for, that the Na Fong Cotton Mill, Japan China Spinning & Weaving
Co., Yatai and Hai Hsin Mills, together with Tachih and Tung Shin
Cotton Mill, have all got on strike, we are to do the same
for our own advantage.

The following are our demands:

1. No insult to our nation.
2. When workers pass in and out of the mills, their
bodies must not be searched.
3. To raise wages by 10% and to pay them promptly.
4. Towards meals no deduction is to be made and
things are to be served to the regular and not discriminated against.
5. The workers are to stay for half an hour for meals.
6. To dismiss the four Japanese foremen (伊藤),
(塚田), (寺家) and (植口).
7. As to the personal property, if it is lost those
responsible are to make good, and if it is stolen those who are
guilty are to be punished.
8. All pay is to be given on time.

If the Japanese illtreat us,
they will lose the market of China. We hope that all the
Chinese will help us in order to hold the national prestige of
China.

The whole body of employees of the
Na Fong Cotton Mill, numbering
more than 4000.
pages.zh:
50分。就我们而言，我们将等待日本资本家
是否真的可以协商。如果他们承诺给予我们最大限度的让步，
鉴于那丰纱厂、日华纺织公司（Japan China Spinning & Weaving Co.）、亚泰（Yatai）和海新（Hai Hsin）纱厂，以及大治（Tachih）和同信（Tung Shin）纱厂都已罢工，为了我们自身的利益，我们也应采取同样的行动。

以下是我们的要求：

1. 不得侮辱我国民族。
2. 工人进出工厂时，不得搜身。
3. 加薪10%，并及时发放。
4. 伙食费不得扣除，供应饭菜应一视同仁，不得歧视。
5. 工人应有半小时用餐时间。
6. 开除四名日本领班：(伊藤)、
(塚田)、(寺家) 和 (植口)。
7. 关于个人财产，如有遗失，责任人须赔偿；如有被盗，罪犯须受惩处。
8. 所有工资须按时发放。

如果日本人虐待我们，
他们将失去中国市场。我们希望所有
中国人都能帮助我们，以维护中国的国家尊严。

那丰纱厂全体雇员，
共计
4000余人。

Further REPORT ON Strike of Cotton Mill Workers in this District.

Made by J. S. Duffield Forwarded by Insptr. Johnston,

Sir,

Further to the reports already forwarded on the strike of cotton mill workers in this district, which commenced on February 14th, I beg to report that the Tai Fong Cotton Mill (大康紗廠), situated at No. 2 Tsungwah Road is still closed.

At the Yue Fong Cotton Mill (裕豐紗廠) situated at No. 90 East Yangtszepoo Road, where 2,920 male and female workers are employed, only 600 workers turned up for work on the day shift, commencing at 6 a.m. February 18th, and only 150 turned up for work on the night shift, commencing at 6 p.m. February 18th. As this was not a sufficient number to carry on the working of the mills, the managements decided to drop the pay books of the workers, who attended with a view to paying them a percentage of their wages.

At 6 a.m. Feb. 19th, only 304 workers turned up for work on the day shift, and the management adopted the same procedure as on Feb. 18th, dropping the books of the workers who attended and allowed them to go home. This means that no work has been done at the Yue Fong Mill since the morning of Feb. 18th.

On Feb. 19th, at 6 a.m. when the shift was going on duty at the Toong Wo Cotton Mill (東華紗廠), situated at No. 87 Ward Road, where 2,900 male and female workers are employed, 140 workers failed to turn up for work, but as they had a sufficient number to perform the duties, work was carried on as usual. At 6.45 a.m., the manager sent a message to the workers who failed to turn up, requesting them to

关于本区棉厂工人罢工的进一步报告。

由 J. S. Duffield 呈报 由 Insptr. Johnston 转呈，

先生：

继之前关于本区棉厂工人罢工的报告（始于2月14日），谨此报告，位于通华路2号的泰丰纱厂（Tai Fong Cotton Mill）* 仍然关闭。

位于东杨树浦路90号的裕丰纱厂（Yue Fong Cotton Mill），雇佣男女工人2,920名，在2月18日上午6点开始的日班中，仅有600名工人到岗，而在2月18日下午6点开始的夜班中，仅有150名工人到岗。由于人数不足以维持工厂运作，管理层决定扣留到岗工人的工资簿，意图向他们支付一定比例的工资。

2月19日上午6点，日班仅有304名工人到岗，管理层采取了与2月18日相同的程序，扣留了到岗工人的工资簿，并允许他们回家。这意味着自2月18日上午以来，裕丰纱厂未进行任何生产工作。

February 17th 1925.

Further REPORT ON Strike at the Dah Kong Cotton Mill, No. 2 Tengyueh Road.

Made by D. S. Grubb Forwarded by Insp. Jumahar

Sir,

I beg to report with reference to the Strike
at the Dah Kong Cotton Mill.

Between 11 a.m. and 2 p.m. Feb. 16th '25, about
1000 male and female strikers attended a meeting at Tseu Ka
Wan (周家湾), about one li north of Ying Ziang Kong, O.O.L.
The strikers were addressed by Tsha Ts Wo (茶之座), School-
teacher, and Woo Sien Tsing (吴先清), female school-teacher,
who stated to them that all their demands (attached to report
of Feb. 14th) had been granted with the exception of Nos.
four and five. The strikers also demanded that those arrested
by the police be released and full pay for the period on
Strike for all. Two of the strikers Tsang Ts Siao (張芝巢),
and Tseu San Ts (周三子) also made speeches at the Meeting.

At 5 p.m. Feb. 16th, two strikers, Tseu Siao
Dah (諸小大) and Si Ka Pau (徐開寶), were arrested while
intimidating about 300 Dah Kong Mill employees at the Mill
Quarters on Pingliang Road. These men with about thirty
others, were preventing the employees from going to work
under threats of assault. They have been charged with intimi-
dation.

At 6 p.m. Feb. 16th, about 120 employees, and
at 6 a.m. Feb. 17th, about 300 employees, reported for work
at the Dah Kong Mill, but were not allowed to start.

Reports have been received from all the Japanese
Mills in the District, expecting the Strike to spread, but
work is still being carried on as usual.

先生，

谨就大康纱厂罢工一事报告如下。

1925年2月16日上午11时至下午2时之间，约1000名男女罢工者在引翔港（Ying Ziang Kong）以北约一里的周家湾（Tseu Ka Wan）参加了一次集会。教师茶之座（Tsha Ts Wo）和女教师吴先清（Woo Sien Tsing）向罢工者发表讲话，称除第四项和第五项外，他们的所有要求（附于2月14日的报告中）均已得到满足。罢工者还要求释放被警方逮捕的人员，并支付罢工期间的全额工资。两名罢工者张芝巢（Tsang Ts Siao）和周三子（Tseu San Ts）也在集会上发了言。

2月16日下午5时，两名罢工者諸小大（Tseu Siao Dah）和徐開寶（Si Ka Pau）在平凉路的工厂宿舍恐吓约300名大康纱厂员工时被逮捕。这些人连同其他约三十人，以殴打相威胁，阻止员工上班。他们已被指控犯有恐吓罪。

2月16日下午6时，约120名员工，以及2月17日上午6时，约300名员工，前往大康纱厂报到上班，但不获准开工。

已收到该区所有日资纱厂的报告，预计罢工会蔓延，但目前工作仍照常进行。

Feb. 16th. 1925

Further REPORT ON strike at the Dah Kong Cotton Mill, No.1 Tengyueh Road.

Made by D. S. Grubb. Forwarded by Insp't. Johnston.

Sir,

I beg to report that during Feb. 15th. no trouble was caused by the strikers of the Dah Kong Cotton Mill, nor no meetings took place inside the settlement in the Yangtsepoo district.

Between 2 and 3 p.m. Feb. 15th., about 300 strikers, both male and female, assembled on a vacant piece of land about one li north of Ying Ziang Kong (引翔港), C. I. L. for the purpose discussing opening negotiations with the Japanese manager of the Dah Kong Cotton Mill, but they were dispersed by Police attached to Ying Ziang Kong Native Police Station. The names of the two principal agitators are ascertained as Tsai Tz' Wu (蔡子華), School teacher, Native Of Honan, who until Feb. 15th. 1925, resided at No. 673 Weichow Road, and Chou San Tz' (周三子), an employee of the Dah Kong Mill. Three female students were also present.

Several strikers, including one Tsang Ts Siao (張芝小), of the Dah Kong Mill, attended a meeting at 11 p.m. Feb. 15th. at Foong San (嵩山路) Road in Frenchtown, where the sign board on the roadway was marked Lau Koong We (勞工會).

At 6 p.m. Feb. 15th. over 300 employees, and 6 a.m. Feb. 16th. about 750 employees, mostly females, entered the Dah Kong Mill with the intention of working, but as this was an insufficient number they were turned out and the manager agreed to pay them a certain percentage of their pay.

I am, Sir,
Yours obediently,
A Grubb
D. S.

D. C. I.

2月15日下午2时至3时之间，约300名男女罢工者在华界引翔港（Ying Ziang Kong）以北约一里的一块空地上集结，目的是讨论与大康纱厂日本经理开启谈判事宜，但被隶属于引翔港中国警察局的警力驱散。查明两名主要煽动者的姓名为蔡子華（Tsai Tz' Wu），教师，河南籍，直至1925年2月15日居住在威州路673号；以及周三子（Chou San Tz'），大康纱厂员工。现场还有三名女学生。

包括大康纱厂的張芝小（Tsang Ts Siao）在内的几名罢工者，参加了2月15日晚11时在法租界嵩山路（Foong San Road）举行的一次集会，路牌上标有“勞工會”（Lau Koong We）。

2月15日下午6时，300多名员工，以及2月16日上午6时，约750名员工（大多为女性）进入大康纱厂意图工作，但由于人数不足，他们被遣散，经理同意支付他们一定比例的工资。

Addendum REPORT ON strike at the Dah Kong Cotton Mill.

Made by D. S. Grubb. Forwarded by [签名]

Sir,

At 6, P. M. on the 14th. February 1925 about 70
night shift employees of the Dah Kong Cotton Mill, entered the
Mill with the intention of working, but as this was an
insufficient number, the Japanese manager decided not to
start the machinery, and agreed to pay the 70 employees at
least half pay and they left satisfied.

There has been no trouble nor demonstration at the
Mill and no outward signs of intimidation so far.

I am, Sir,
Yours obediently,
M. Grubb
D. S.

WA
